writePaths.idempotencyGuard: No client-side state at all: the script re-scans the 45-day window and re-POSTs every distinct order every 15 minutes. The only guard is server-side: (a) purchase-row status latch — full credit fires only when assignedRow.status !== 'delivered' && body.status === 'delivered' && body totalQty > 0 (migrate.js 192-194), or on auto-assign when body.status === 'delivered' (239-241); (b) BRACKET_STATUS_RANK upgrade-only rule (79, 169) so a row never goes back to in_route; (c) self-heal delta fires only when wasDelivered && stored qtys !== body qtys (195-200). order_total/estimated_delivery updates are filtered .is(null) so they no-op after first fill.
writePaths.notes: CREDIT AMOUNT COMES FROM THE POST BODY, NOT THE STORED ROW (193-194, 240): a delivery email whose merged payload has qty 0 (confirmation email outside the 45-day window, archived out of INBOX — scan is INBOX-only, script 180 — or in a mailbox that failed that run) flips the row to delivered (185 statusPatch) with NO credit, and the latch then blocks any future credit. ORDER OF OPERATIONS: inventory adjust (193) runs BEFORE the purchase-row status update (203); the update's error is only recorded in results (204), not thrown, so a failed status write re-credits on the next 15-min run until it succeeds. adjustBracketInventory discards the select error (86) and never checks insert/update errors (90, 96), so a failed inventory write = 'delivered but never credited'. Self-heal (195-200) applies (body - stored) as a signed delta clamped at 0: because mergeByOrder takes MAX qty across every email in the rolling 45-day window (script 103-105), the merged qty can DROP when the confirmation email ages out while a delivery/partial-shipment email that lists fewer items stays in-window, producing a DEBIT; conversely any single over-parse in the window inflates the stored qty and the inventory permanently. canceled (rank 2 > delivered) upgrades a delivered row's status but there is no inventory claw-back anywhere in bracketSync. Endpoint accepts either Authorization: Bearer CRON_SECRET or ?secret= (841-843). No concurrency group on the workflow, so overlapping runs can both read status=in_route and both credit.

FIX: li_rev optimistic lock — 409 if body.li_rev missing/stale, CAS claim via casBumpLiRev before the rewrite, second CAS 'seal' after, using a FRESH metadata read so completion stamps (bracket_deducted_at) written in the window are not reverted (api/admin.js bookingLineItemsSave diff @@ -4395,+4360..+4380, +4413..+4442, +4486..+4510; api/tech.js jobLineItemsSave @@ +709..+745, +866..+874); every outside-editor writer (GDS upsell, cash tax strip, mirror.js, Zenbooker backfill) bumps li_rev; new api/_lib/line-items.js clampBracketQtysToTvCount (lines 154-206: only trims when a category has >=2 lines with >=1 non-selection label, else warns and stands down) wired into BOTH detectBracketQtys copies (admin.js @@ +11996..+12000; tech.js @@ +1761..+1765); tech status() now re-reads metadata before writing wire_plate_deducted_at (tech.js @@ -833,+959..+965). STRUCTURAL: bracket consumption is DERIVED by regex over free-text line-item names (no structured bracket field on the ticket), so any duplicate or hand-typed line changes the deduction; line items were replaced by unlocked blind full-rewrites; the idempotency stamps live in one JSONB metadata blob that several handlers overwrite whole (last-writer-wins) — a stale copy can erase bracket_deducted_at and re-arm a deduction; clamp logic is a fourth piece duplicated into two files with 'keep in sync' comments.

3b1183a (2026-09-02, 'Close two live bracket-inventory-tracking gaps') — BROKEN: (1) office bookingUpdate completion silently skipped deduct+stamp+log whenever the booking had neither technician_id nor bracket_supplied_by (the `if (supplier)` from ba87325 had no else); (2) bookingLineItemsSave never touched bracket accounting, so adding/removing bracket lines on a completed ticket left counter and ledger permanently stale. FIX: (1) else-branch inserts an unattributed bracket_usage_logs row (technician_id null, real qtys, 'inventory NOT deducted, needs manual attribution') and deliberately leaves bracket_deducted_at unset (api/admin.js diff @@ +4358..+4374); (2) when bracket_deducted_at is stamped, diff detectBracketQtys(oldRows) vs (items) and call adjustBracketInventory(+1 old) then (-1 new) against bracket_supplied_by||technician_id, warn if none (admin.js @@ +4639..+4670). Only admin.js changed — whether api/tech.js jobLineItemsSave reconciles is outside what this commit touched; I did not verify it. The commit message also records a Sept-2 data backfill run DIRECTLY in Supabase (no commit, no script in scripts/) that retroactively decremented 13 pre-ba87325 jobs — the backfill that collided with the Jul-7 raw-SQL baseline reset (ba87325's fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql) and produced today's double-deduction for TK/Greg/Juan/Steve. STRUCTURAL: consumption protocol (resolve supplier, adjust, stamp, log) is re-implemented per writer so each new writer re-discovers a gap; 'no supplier' silently dropped the event for two months; the +1/-1 revert-and-recharge pattern re-clamps at 0 on the +1 side, so a decrement that was previously clamped gets over-restored; the backfill was a raw bypass with no ledger to consult for the earlier raw reset it needed to know about — ledger not source of truth + raw SQL bypass compounding.

RECURRING STRUCTURAL CAUSES (3-4 across all 11 commits): (1) ONE MUTABLE COUNTER, MANY UNCOORDINATED WRITERS — over ten weeks the same bracket_inventory row was mutated by tech status(), office bookingUpdate(), jobBracketSetSupplier, office bookingLineItemsSave, admin bracketUpdate set/adjust/usage, bracketAssign, bracketSync auto-assign + self-heal, the temp tech bracketInventorySet, and at least four raw SQL/direct-DB edits; every fix ADDED a path rather than funnelling through one. (2) LOGIC DUPLICATED IN THREE FILES — adjustBracketInventory exists in api/admin.js, api/tech.js and api/migrate.js, detectBracketQtys and the TV-count clamp in two; each fix (home-business key 5199678, ledger 7b166cb, clamp 1959e92) landed on some copies and not others (migrate.js:84 at HEAD has neither the home-business resolution nor a ledger insert). (3) NO REAL IDEMPOTENCY KEY / NON-ATOMIC READ-MODIFY-WRITE — guards are a JSONB metadata stamp written in a separate round-trip after the counter update, a status transition observed in a read, or a stored-qty diff; the metadata blob is overwritten whole by several handlers (last-writer-wins), and Math.max(0) clamping silently swallows decrements then over-restores on revert — so the same event can fire twice or half-fire. (4) LEDGER NOT SOURCE OF TRUTH + RAW SQL BYPASS — bracket_usage_logs was bolted on 2026-08-21 as a best-effort side effect with unsigned columns, sign in free text, manual sets logged as zeros, and keyed by the job's business while the counter is keyed by the tech's home business, so it can never be summed to rebuild the counter; meanwhile 48c9475 (Juan +5 upsert), ba87325 (TK/Greg baseline reset), 5199678 (phantom-row delete) and the Sept-2 Supabase backfill all changed counts with no ledger row, which is exactly why the Sept-2 backfill could not see that the Jul-7 reset had already absorbed those July jobs.

findings.title: Owner marks an auto-assigned in-route order 'Delivered' by hand → brackets are NEVER credited (latch set, sync will not credit)
findings.scenario: 1. Walmart order ships to TK's home (10507/80022). 2. Cron parses the confirmation email; bracketSync has no assigned row, matchTechByAddress hits TECH_HOME_ADDRESSES → matched branch stamps technician_id=TK with status in_route and credits nothing (migrate.js:179, 214-235; line 239 requires status==='delivered'). 3. Package arrives but Walmart's 'Your package arrived' email never parses (different template, lands in an unscanned mailbox, or was archived out of INBOX — the scanner reads INBOX only, bracket-email-sync.mjs:180). 4. TK tells the office he has the brackets. Owner opens Inventory tab, sees '🚚 In route', picks '✓ Delivered' in the Status dropdown (admin.html:11319-11323 → setBracketStatus → admin.js bracketSetStatus 12058-12075). That handler updates ONLY bracket_purchases.status/delivered_date (12069-12073) — no bracket_inventory write, no ledger row. 5. Next cron run (≤15 min, and every run for 45 days): assignedRow.status is now 'delivered' → wasDelivered=true (migrate.js:183) → the credit condition `!wasDelivered && nowDelivered` at 192 is false; the heal at 195 only fires if the email qty differs from the row qty (187) → no-op. 6. Same outcome via the GitHub 'Manual status override' (bracket-tracker.yml:39-56): it POSTs {walmart_order_num, status} with no quantities → totalQty=0 → 192 false, but the status flips (185, 203) and the latch is set forever. Result: the physical brackets are on TK's truck; his count never went up.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows FEWER than physical by the full order quantity (e.g. 0/3/2 fewer flat/tilting/full_motion) permanently; only a manual 'set' in the Edit modal can fix it
findings.structuralCause: bracket_purchases.status is doing double duty as both 'what the email said' and 'has this order been credited'. bracketSetStatus and the workflow override can set status without moving inventory, and bracketSync then reads status as proof-of-credit. There is no `credited` column on bracket_purchases (migration 0029:20-33) — the wire-plate twin got one in 0041 and wirePlateSetStatus credits/claws back behind it (admin.js:12036-12051); the bracket control was never given the same behaviour.
findings.alreadyHappened: No direct evidence for brackets. Adjacent evidence: 77cc7e0 (2026-07-26) added the same manual dropdown for wire plates precisely because 'Amazon doesn't always send that email' — the office relies on the manual flip when the delivery email fails, which is exactly the trigger here. 7dc27f9 (2026-07-21) shows assigned in-route orders sit long enough to need low-stock suppression.

findings.title: Owner downgrades a delivered order to 'In route' → next cron re-credits the full order (double credit) and silently flips it back
findings.scenario: 1. An auto-assigned order (Greg, 9600/80231) is delivered; the delivery email flips the assigned row in_route→delivered and credits Greg the full qty (migrate.js:192-194, status persisted at 203). 2. Owner believes the credit was wrong (Greg says one box is missing, or the owner wants to 'undo' and redo the count) and picks '🚚 In route' from the Status dropdown (admin.html:11319-11323). bracketSetStatus sets status='in_route', delivered_date=null on every row for that order number (admin.js:12069-12073) — no inventory claw-back. 3. Within 15 minutes the cron re-scans; the delivery email is still inside the 45-day INBOX window so the same payload (status=delivered, full qty) is POSTed again (bracket-email-sync.mjs:181, 311-330). 4. bracketSync: assignedRow.status='in_route' → wasDelivered=false, nowDelivered=true, totalQty>0 → adjustBracketInventory adds the FULL order quantity a second time (migrate.js:192-194) and status returns to delivered (203). 5. Owner sees the status has reverted on its own; Greg's count is now one order too high and there is no ledger row for either credit.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows MORE than physical by the full order quantity, once per downgrade; the owner's status change is undone within 15 minutes
findings.structuralCause: Same root as C1 in the other direction: the sync's only idempotency memory is the mutable status column, the scanner re-POSTs every order every 15 minutes for 45 days with no client-side 'seen' state, and the manual status control edits that column without touching inventory. Any status write from outside the sync re-arms the credit.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Assigning a Handy Andy tech from the Dom's tab (possible since 2026-09-02) → delivery credit lands on a phantom row under Dom's; the tech's real row and every deduction never see it
findings.scenario: 1. Unknown-address order is mirrored unassigned to both businesses (migrate.js:248-274). 2. Owner is on the Dom's tab. Since 3f80949 (2026-09-02) the Inventory tab lists every business's techs (admin.js:11826-11833, .in('business_id', bizIds)) and the Assign modal builds its dropdown from that list (admin.html:11088 `window._bracketInv=inv.inventory`, 11029-11030). Owner picks Steve (Handy Andy) for the Dom's mirrored row. 3. bracketAssign stamps the DOM'S row technician_id=Steve (admin.js:12566-12568), deletes the unassigned HA twin (12576-12580, `.neq('business_id', bizId)` where bizId=Dom's), and because status is in_route credits nothing (12587 `credited = purchase.status === 'delivered'`; response reserved:true). 4. Delivery email arrives → bracketSync: rows=[Dom's row, technician_id=Steve] → assigned branch → adjustBracketInventory(db, assignedRow.business_id /*Dom's*/, Steve) (migrate.js:193). No (Dom's, Steve) inventory row exists → INSERT a new row holding the order qty (migrate.js:89-93). Steve's real (HA, Steve) row is untouched. 5. Steve completes a job: both deduct helpers resolve his HOME business (admin.js:12271-12275, tech.js:1789-1793) and decrement the HA row → clamps at 0 while the Dom's phantom row still holds the delivered brackets. 6. Tech app reads (auth.tech_id, auth.business_id=HA) (tech.js:2500-2501) → Steve never sees the delivery. Inventory tab shows 'Steve (handy-andy) 0/0/0' with a reorder chip AND 'Steve (doms) 0/0/4'.
findings.wrongBy: tech's real row shows FEWER than physical by the full order qty; a second row under the wrong company holds them; subsequent completions clamp at 0 so the shortfall compounds and is never recoverable from the ledger (sync writes no ledger row)
findings.structuralCause: Three writers key the same physical stock three ways: bracketAssign (post-3f80949) and the auto-assign matched branch (migrate.js:240) credit the tech's home business; the sync's assigned branch credits the PURCHASE ROW's business_id (migrate.js:193, 196); the tech app reads by token business. 3f80949 changed admin.js to allow cross-tab assignment but api/migrate.js has not been touched since a0432fb (2026-08-20), so the sync still assumes row business == tech business. The unique (business_id, technician_id) key on bracket_inventory guarantees a second row instead of an error.
findings.alreadyHappened: The phantom-row class has happened: 5199678 (2026-07-16) fixed 'TK (a Doms tech) completed a Handy Andy job → phantom always-zero row (TK/handy-andy) → false reorder alert, real Doms row never decremented', cleaned up by hand in the DB with no script. This credit-side variant became reachable on 2026-09-02 (3f80949) and has no evidence of firing yet.

findings.title: Canceled after delivery credit → brackets stay on the count forever; a false 'cancel' word on an in-route order blocks its credit forever
findings.scenario: A. 1. Order delivered and credited (migrate.js:192-194 or bracketAssign admin.js:12587-12608). 2. Owner returns/refunds it or Walmart cancels a partial; either a Walmart cancellation email arrives or the owner picks 'Canceled' in the dropdown. 3. Sync: canceled ranks 2 > delivered 1 (migrate.js:79) → upgrades() true → statusPatch only (185, 203). There is NO negative branch in bracketSync for a cancel: the only debit path is the qty-heal at 195-200, which requires wasDelivered && qtyChanged with totalQty>0 (187) — a cancel email/override carries the same or zero quantities. bracketSetStatus likewise sets status only (admin.js:12069-12073). 4. Row is now terminal (nothing ranks above 2) so no later run can touch it. Count exceeds physical by the canceled qty forever. Migration 0029's own header promises 'When Walmart cancels: decrement inventory by canceled qty' (0029:12) — never implemented; the wire-plate twin does claw back (admin.js:12036-12039). B. 1. Order in route, auto-assigned. 2. A forwarded thread or Walmart footer containing the bare word 'cancel' (e.g. 'to cancel your order') is parsed — detectStatus's regex `/cancel(?:l?ed|lation)?\b/` (walmart-parse.mjs:68) makes the suffix optional so 'cancel' alone matches, and it runs before the delivered test (72). 3. mergeByOrder keeps the highest rank (script 106) → payload status=canceled every run. 4. bracketSync upgrades the row to canceled (185, 203); when the real delivery email arrives its 'delivered' can never out-rank 'canceled' (169), so 192 never fires. Physical delivery, count never goes up, and the owner's dropdown offers no path back (setting Delivered leaves wasDelivered=true on the next run, see C1).
findings.wrongBy: A: tech shows MORE than physical by the canceled order qty, permanently. B: tech shows FEWER than physical by the full order qty, permanently
findings.structuralCause: The status ladder is monotonic and the credit is one-way: 'canceled' is treated as a terminal label rather than an event with an inventory consequence. No signed movement is recorded anywhere for a credit, so there is nothing to reverse; and because the same column is the idempotency latch, a wrong terminal status also locks out the correct future event.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence for brackets; the parser's cancel regex has been unchanged since e35f347 (2026-06-29). Whether Walmart delivery/marketing emails contain the bare word 'cancel' is not recorded in the repo.

findings.title: bracket_parse_email credits at order time AND on every re-submit, then the cron credits the same order again at delivery
findings.scenario: 1. Owner (or anything holding an owner token — there is no UI caller; grep finds only the dispatch at admin.js:460) POSTs bracket_parse_email {technician_name:'tk', walmart_order_num, full_motion_qty:2}. 2. admin.js:12448-12456 inserts a bracket_purchases row WITH technician_id=TK and WITHOUT a status (DB default 'ordered' = rank 0, 0029:28); 12461-12480 immediately adds +2 FM to TK's inventory — no ledger row, every DB error discarded, response says inventory_updated regardless. 3. The same Walmart order's emails are also in the scanned INBOX. Cron → bracketSync: rows now contain a technician_id → assigned branch; wasDelivered=false ('ordered'); when the merged status is delivered (immediately if the delivery email is already in the window) → 192-194 credits +2 FM AGAIN. 4. If the owner re-POSTs to fix a typo, the 'updated' branch (12437-12445) runs and 12461-12480 credits the full qty a THIRD time — the credit is unconditional on both branches. 5. Amplifier: if the cron had already mirrored this order to both businesses unassigned, bracketParseEmail's lookup is per business (12417-12418), so it may create a SECOND assigned row in the other business; bracketSync then picks assignedRow with `rows.find` on an un-ordered query (163-165, 177) — run N can credit via row A (→delivered), run N+1 via row B (still in_route → credit again) while the twin-delete at 209-213 skips both because both have technician_id.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows MORE than physical by 1× the order qty per parse-email call plus 1× at sync delivery (2×–3× total)
findings.structuralCause: Two crediting policies coexist in one codebase — credit-at-order (bracketParseEmail, never updated after 3e13303 moved everything else to credit-on-delivery) and credit-on-first-delivered-transition (bracketSync/bracketAssign) — and neither writes a marker the other can read. bracket_purchases has no unique key on (business_id, walmart_order_num) and no credited flag, so 'one order' can be N rows in N states.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence — endpoint has had no caller since the tracker was folded into migrate.js (85ff97b, 2026-06-28); it is live and owner-token reachable.

findings.title: Two scanner runs overlap (manual workflow_dispatch + cron, no concurrency group) or the status write fails after the credit → same delivery credited twice
findings.scenario: 1. Cron run A starts at :00 (bracket-tracker.yml:11). 2. At :00:30 the owner clicks 'Run workflow' to set a status / add a zip / send an SMS test — the manual step runs first, then the job proceeds to the full email scan anyway (yml:70-119; the scan step has no `if:`) as run B. The workflow has no `concurrency:` key, so A and B run in parallel. 3. Both scan the same INBOXes, build the same merged order list in the same order, and POST bracket_sync for the same just-delivered order ~seconds apart. 4. Request A: reads rows (migrate.js:163-165) → in_route → passes 192 → adjustBracketInventory reads inv (86-88) → writes +qty (96-100) → THEN persists status=delivered (203). Request B started before A reached 203, so its rows read also shows in_route and it passes 192; its inventory read at 86 happens after A's write at 96 → B adds +qty on top → double credit. (If B's inventory read precedes A's write the result is a lost update — one credit — by luck.) 5. Independent variant, single run: if the update at 203 errors or the Vercel function is cut off between 194 and 203, the credit stands, the row stays in_route (error only pushed into results at 204, not thrown), and every subsequent 15-minute run re-credits until the status write finally sticks. The GitHub job still shows green because per-order POST failures are only console.error'd (bracket-email-sync.mjs:327-329) and main() exits 0.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows MORE than physical by the full order qty per overlapping pair / per failed status write
findings.structuralCause: Credit-before-latch ordering (inventory at 193, status at 203) in a JS read-modify-write with no transaction, no conditional UPDATE (`.eq('status','in_route')`), and no atomic increment; combined with a scanner that has no client-side dedupe state and a workflow that permits concurrent runs. wirePlateSync has the same ordering but at least persists a dedicated `credited` boolean in the same patch; brackets have neither.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Rolling 45-day window turns a parse difference between confirmation and delivery emails into a silent debit (or credit) weeks after delivery
findings.scenario: 1. Day 0: confirmation email parses 'quantity 3 item onn Tilting TV Wall Mount' → tilting=3 (walmart-parse.mjs:50-52). 2. Day 5: 'Your package arrived' email lists the product without the 'quantity N item' structure → fallback regex counts ONE per '<type> … Wall Mount' phrase (walmart-parse.mjs:55-58) → tilting=1, status delivered. 3. Days 5–45: mergeByOrder keeps max per type across both emails (bracket-email-sync.mjs:103-105) → payload tilting=3 → row credited 3 on first delivered flip (migrate.js:192-194), then every run is a no-op (qtyChanged false). 4. Day 46: the confirmation email ages out of the search window (LOOKBACK_DAYS=45, script 37, 181) while the delivery email is still inside it → merged payload becomes tilting=1, delivered. 5. bracketSync: wasDelivered=true, totalQty=1>0, row qty 3 !== 1 → qtyChanged (187) → heal delta −2 (195-200) → adjustBracketInventory subtracts 2 tilting (clamped at 0 at 85) and overwrites the row qty to 1 (188). The tech physically still has all 3. Mirror image: any email inside the window that OVER-parses (a forwarded thread whose segmentation fails, a recommendation block naming a bracket type near 'wall mount') raises the max and is credited straight into inventory through the same heal with no review, and sticks. Caveat: this depends on how Walmart's delivery email formats its item list, which the repo does not record — the parser header says it was built against the confirmation email only (walmart-parse.mjs:4-7).
findings.wrongBy: tech shows FEWER than physical by (confirmation qty − delivery-email parsed qty) per type, appearing ~45 days after the order with no ledger row; or MORE by any over-parse
findings.structuralCause: The credit amount is derived by regex from whichever emails happen to be in a sliding window, merged with max(), and the server treats any difference from the stored row as a physical correction to apply immediately (self-heal). There is no notion of 'quantity confirmed by the confirmation email' vs 'quantity mentioned in a later notice', and no human review step before inventory moves.
findings.alreadyHappened: Parse-driven inventory moves have happened: c722678 (2026-06-28) fixed a text+html double-count that had already parsed live order 2000147 as 2/6/2 instead of 1/3/1, and 17a4b5d (same day) added the self-heal specifically to push corrected parse quantities into inventory. The 45-day age-out variant has no evidence.

findings.title: Jul-7 policy switch: orders auto-assigned and credited at ASSIGNMENT under 65c3f82 were credited again at DELIVERY under 3e13303 (no data correction shipped, no credited marker to stop it)
findings.scenario: 1. 2026-07-07 17:28 UTC, 65c3f82 deploys auto-assign-by-address; its matched branch credits `if (totalQty > 0)` regardless of status (visible in the 65c3f82 diff: '// Credit the tech's inventory by the order quantity (first-and-only credit)'). Cron was hourly at that point (60bf631). 2. An in-route order shipping to a known tech home (TK/Greg via Dom's; Steve/Juan/Kregg/Zach via HA) is scanned in that window → auto-assigned AND credited while still in route. The owner notices counts ahead of the truck and flags it — 3e13303's message: 'Inventory was credited when an order was assigned (incl. my new auto-assign), before the brackets were actually delivered.' 3. 18:47 UTC, 3e13303 changes the rule to credit on the in_route→delivered transition (migrate.js:192-194) and changes the matched branch to credit only if already delivered (239). The commit touches only api/admin.js, api/migrate.js, public/admin.html — no SQL, no data fix — and bracket_purchases has no column recording that the early credit happened (0029:20-33). 4. That order's delivery email arrives days later → assigned branch: wasDelivered=false, nowDelivered=true → full credit a second time. 5. Unlike the debit-side incident, the same-day raw-SQL baseline reset (ba87325, 04:54 UTC) ran BEFORE the auto-assign commit, so TK's/Greg's 'physical count' reset could not have absorbed this; any Jul-7 in-flight order for them would have been credited twice on top of the reset.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows MORE than physical by the full order qty for each order that was in route and auto-assigned between 17:28 and 18:47 UTC on 2026-07-07 (or in the one hourly scan inside that window)
findings.structuralCause: A behavioural change to when a credit fires was deployed without recording, per order, whether the old rule had already fired — because there is no 'credited' marker on bracket_purchases and no ledger row for credits, the new code could not distinguish 'in_route and never credited' from 'in_route but credited at assignment an hour ago'. The only way to know is the owner's memory.
findings.alreadyHappened: Partially confirmed by git: the FIRST (premature) credit is attested by the 3e13303 commit message ('owner flagged'). Whether any such order was later re-credited at delivery, or manually corrected via the Set modal, cannot be determined from the repo; no correction script exists for it (unlike Juan's 48c9475 the same morning).

findings.title: Raw-SQL physical reset has no representation anywhere, so the Sept-2 retroactive backfill re-deducted jobs the July-7 reset had already absorbed
findings.scenario: 1) Jul 1-6: TK, Greg, Juan and Steve complete solo jobs; the code at that time (pre-ba87325) never deducts brackets on solo jobs and never writes metadata.bracket_deducted_at. 2) Jul 7 04:24-04:54 UTC: owner counts the trucks and pastes scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql into the Supabase SQL editor (TK full_motion_qty=1 at :14-18, Greg 3/2/2 at :21-25) and scripts/fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql STEP 3 (+5/+5/+5 at :34-41, on top of an earlier undocumented 'reset to 0', comment :32). Neither statement writes a bracket_usage_logs row; bracket_inventory has no counted_at/snapshot column (0029:46-55); the ledger did not exist as a side effect until 7b166cb on Aug 21. 3) Sep 2: owner audits Juan's count, selects completed bookings whose metadata lacks bracket_deducted_at, finds 13 pre-ba87325 jobs, and applies their detectBracketQtys deduction directly in Supabase (3b1183a commit message: 'the other 13 ... got their real decrement applied retroactively'). 4) Those 13 jobs were already reflected in the Jul-7 physical numbers, so each tech's count drops by the July usage a second time.
findings.wrongBy: TK, Greg, Juan and Steve each show FEWER brackets than physical by the full bracket qtys of their pre-Jul-7 jobs among the 13 backfilled (a second deduction of consumption the reset had already absorbed)
codeRefs: git 3b1183a (commit message: 13 jobs decremented retroactively, done directly in Supabase)
git ba87325 (fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql shipped in the same commit that turned on auto-decrement)
findings.structuralCause: The only per-booking idempotency memory is metadata.bracket_deducted_at, and a physical reset has no memory at all: no ledger row, no 'counted_at' on bracket_inventory, no 'everything before T is absorbed' marker. Any later replay of pre-reset events (a backfill keyed on the missing stamp) is therefore guaranteed to double-apply them, and nothing in the DB can warn the person doing the backfill.
findings.alreadyHappened: Yes: this is the 2026-09-03 incident. git shows both raw scripts committed Jul 7 (48c9475, ba87325) and 3b1183a (Sep 2) records the raw Supabase backfill of 13 pre-ba87325 jobs.

findings.title: A UI 'Set Brackets' reset is just as invisible to a later backfill as raw SQL: its ledger row carries zeros, no booking link, and the absorbed job stays unstamped
findings.scenario: 1) Office marks a Zenbooker-imported job 'completed' from the dashboard while it has no technician_id and no bracket_supplied_by (Steve did it, nobody assigned him). admin.js 4355-4384 takes the else-branch: it inserts an unattributed bracket_usage_logs row with the real qtys (technician_id null) and deliberately leaves bracket_deducted_at UNSET (4372-4375). Before 3b1183a the same job silently skipped everything, per that commit's message. Inventory does not move. 2) Two days later the owner counts Steve's truck, opens Inventory > Edit (admin.html 11443-11455), types the real numbers and saves. bracketUpdate 'set' (admin.js 12115-12118, 12140-12148) overwrites the row; the ledger row at 12165-12169 sets NO flat_used/tilting_used/full_motion_used (DB default 0, 0029:72-74), booking_id is null because the UI never sends one (11476-11483), and the before/after lives only in notes text 'manual set by office: tilting 4->2'. Steve's physical count already reflects the job. 3) Later the office assigns Steve for payroll: Reopen (admin.html 3387 -> admin.js 4129-4142, metadata copied without a stamp), pick Steve, Mark complete (3386 -> 4144-4155). 4349 sees no bracket_deducted_at and deducts the job's qtys from Steve again. Same outcome if the next audit re-runs the Sept-2 method ('completed bookings with no stamp'). 4) Steve's count is now below physical by the job's brackets.
findings.wrongBy: Tech shows N fewer of each bracket type than physical, where N = the qtys of every unstamped completed job the owner's physical set had already absorbed
findings.structuralCause: A manual set records a free-text before/after instead of a signed delta and never links to the bookings it absorbs; the code's own recovery design (leave unstamped so a later recomplete deducts 'for real') assumes no manual reset happened in between, and nothing can tell it otherwise. Sets made between c3cc358 (Jun 30) and 7b166cb (Aug 21) have no ledger row at all.
findings.alreadyHappened: Partially: the no-supplier office completion gap was live until 3b1183a (Sep 2) and TK's Aug-21 drift investigation (7b166cb message) found manual sets with no history; no direct evidence of the reopen-after-set replay yet.

findings.title: Set Brackets modal overwrites all three columns from render-time values, silently reverting an automatic deduction that landed while the modal was open
findings.scenario: 1) Office opens the Inventory tab; TK shows flat 5 / tilting 2 / full_motion 4. Office clicks Edit on TK to bump flat to 7 (two brackets handed over in person); the modal is prefilled with 5/2/4 (admin.html 11443-11455). 2) While the modal is open, TK taps Complete on a 1x Full Motion job: tech.js 980-997 -> adjustBracketInventory (1791-1800) sets full_motion 4->3, writes an auto-deduct ledger row and the stamp. 3) Office types 7 in flat and clicks Save. saveBracketCount posts {flat:7, tilting:2, full_motion:4, action:'set'} (11472-11483). bracketUpdate reads the row (full_motion now 3, 12099-12100), computes isSet -> fullMotion=4 (12118) and writes all three columns (12140-12148). The ledger row reads 'manual set by office: flat 5->7, full_motion 3->4'. 4) TK's count shows full_motion 4 while the truck holds 3, and the ledger makes the reversal look like a deliberate owner correction.
findings.wrongBy: Tech shows 1 more full_motion (or whichever type the concurrent job used) than physical per job completed while the modal was open; the ledger records it as an intentional +1
findings.structuralCause: Absolute 'set' of every bracket column from stale client state with no per-column change detection and no compare-and-swap on updated_at; the automatic deduction and the manual set are two uncoordinated writers on one mutable counter.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: A manual reset followed by a supplier change or a line-item reconcile re-applies the original job quantities on top of the reset (restore assumes the deduction is still in the count)
findings.scenario: A) 1) Two-tech job (TK primary, Greg helper) with 2x tilting; TK taps Complete -> tech.js 992 deducts 2 tilting from TK (5->3) and stamps bracket_deducted_at. 2) Greg actually pulled the brackets from his own truck. Owner counts TK's truck next morning: 5. Owner opens Set Brackets and sets TK tilting=5 (ledger: 'manual set by office: tilting 3->5'). 3) That afternoon Greg opens the job in the tech app and records himself as supplier (tech.html 1246 -> tech.js jobBracketSetSupplier). Because bracket_deducted_at is set (1237), line 1238 restores +2 tilting to TK (5->7) and 1239 charges Greg -2, both with qtys recomputed from the CURRENT line items (1226), not the amount originally moved. 4) TK shows 7 tilting; the truck holds 5. B) Office variant: a completed job auto-deducted 2 tilting but only 1 was used; owner resets TK to physical; office later corrects the ticket to 1 tilting -> admin.js 4658-4671 restores +2 then charges -1 -> TK is 1 above physical. C) Aggravator with no reset at all: if the original deduction was clamped at 0 (tech.js 1796-1798, recorded only as a WARNING string at 1821-1822), the +2 restore in A manufactures two brackets from nothing.
findings.wrongBy: Previous supplier shows the full original job qty MORE than physical (A, C); tech shows (old qty - new qty) more than physical (B)
findings.structuralCause: The 'restore old, charge new' pattern treats the running count as still containing the original deduction and reverses a recomputed quantity rather than a recorded signed movement; a manual set (or a clamp) breaks that invariant and nothing records that a booking's deduction was absorbed or truncated.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence of the reset+restore sequence; clamped deductions are documented as having happened (7b166cb message: TK's Jul 1/3/6 jobs)

findings.title: No usable per-booking idempotency key for backfills: the stamp can be absent, erased by a whole-metadata write, or stripped by reopen, and ledger rows cannot stand in for it
findings.scenario: 1) The Sept-2 backfill applied 13 deductions with raw SQL (3b1183a: 'done directly, no code change'). If it did not also write metadata.bracket_deducted_at, those 13 jobs remain 'completed + unstamped'. 2) Office opens one of them to fix an address, taps Reopen (admin.html 3387 -> admin.js 4129-4142: status->assigned, metadata copied minus late-alert keys, no stamp) then Mark complete (3386 -> 4144-4155). 4349 finds no stamp -> adjustBracketInventory deducts the job a THIRD time. 3) Any future backfill that instead keys on 'does a bracket_usage_logs row exist for this booking' is wrong both ways: the 61 jobs deducted before 7b166cb have a stamp but no ledger row (3b1183a message) and would be re-deducted; a job completed with no supplier has an unattributed ledger row with real qtys but no deduction (4377-4382) and would be skipped; a job later re-completed after a supplier is set gets a second row (4362 -> 12296-12302) and would be counted twice; 'restore' rows store positive *_used (12298) and would read as consumption. There is no uniqueness on the ledger (0029:79-80). 4) Even a correct stamp can vanish: bookingLineItemsSave reads metadata at 4518 and passes that object to casBumpLiRev at 4590, which rewrites the WHOLE metadata guarded only on li_rev (line-items.js 219-222); a completion that stamped between 4518 and 4590 is reverted (the seal at 4697-4701 was fixed for exactly this, the claim was not), and the next reopen->recomplete deducts again.
findings.wrongBy: Tech shows the job's bracket qtys fewer than physical for every extra replay of a completed job; a ledger-keyed backfill would additionally re-deduct the 61 stamped-but-unlogged jobs and skip the unattributed ones
codeRefs: git 3b1183a (61 jobs stamped before the ledger existed; 13 backfilled raw)
findings.structuralCause: Idempotency lives in a JSONB key that several handlers overwrite whole and that raw SQL may or may not set; the ledger has no signed delta, no row kind, and no (booking_id, technician_id, kind) uniqueness, so neither the stamp nor the ledger can be trusted as the key for a replay.
findings.alreadyHappened: The backfill itself happened Sep 2 (3b1183a); whether it stamped the 13 bookings is not recorded anywhere in the repo, which is itself the finding. No evidence yet of the reopen->recomplete triple deduction.

findings.title: The raw fix scripts remain in the repo as re-runnable absolute writes with name-prefix matching, no business filter, and no ledger row
findings.scenario: 1) In September someone follows the file's own instructions ('Add more techs below as you count them', template at :27-31) and re-runs scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql to re-baseline one tech, leaving the TK/Greg statements in place: Greg is set back to 3/2/2 (July numbers) and TK's full_motion to 1 regardless of the current count (:14-25), matching `t.name ilike 'greg%'` / `'tk%'` across every business (no business_id filter). No bracket_usage_logs row is written. 2) Re-running scripts/fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql STEP 3 adds another +5/+5/+5 (`on conflict do update ... + 5`, :38-41) for every 'juan%' tech in every business (:34-37). 3) STEP 2 (:21-29) marks order 2000149-97869279 delivered with qty 5/5/5 so bracketSync will not re-credit (migrate.js 183-192), but if the 15-min scanner later parses that order's email with different quantities (fallback of one-per-type at walmart-parse.mjs 55-58) the heal branch (migrate.js 187-188, 195-200) applies email-minus-5 per type to Juan's inventory with no ledger row (migrate.js 84-101 never touches bracket_usage_logs). 4) Counts diverge from physical by whatever moved since July (Greg/TK) or by +15 per extra run (Juan).
findings.wrongBy: Greg/TK reset to the July-7 numbers, i.e. off by every credit and deduction since Jul 7; Juan +15 brackets per extra STEP-3 run, or up to -12 if the scanner heals against the 5/5/5 row
findings.structuralCause: Ad-hoc raw SQL against the mutable counter with no run-once guard, no ledger side effect, and lookups by name prefix instead of technician id; the repo actively invites more of the same via the template comment.
findings.alreadyHappened: Both scripts were committed and run once on Jul 7 (git 48c9475, ba87325; the Juan comment references an earlier undocumented reset to 0). No evidence of a re-run.

findings.title: A manual physical-count correction after an over-credited Walmart delivery is silently undone by the email sync's self-heal when the higher-qty email ages out of the 45-day window
findings.scenario: 1) Walmart confirmation email for an assigned order is parsed as 6 tilting (double-count or recommendation-block over-parse; mergeByOrder keeps the MAX per type across all in-window emails, bracket-email-sync.mjs 98-113). 2) Delivery email arrives; bracketSync flips in_route->delivered and credits +6 tilting to the tech and stores 6 on the purchase row (migrate.js 187-188, 192-194). 3) Owner counts the truck, sees only 3 arrived, opens Set Brackets and lowers tilting by 3 (ledger 'manual set by office: tilting 9->6'). Physical and count now agree. 4) ~45 days after the confirmation email (LOOKBACK_DAYS=45, bracket-email-sync.mjs 37) it ages out of the INBOX scan while the later delivery email is still in-window; if that email parses fewer items (fallback counts one per type-word, walmart-parse.mjs 55-58) the merged qty drops to 3 or 1. bracketSync's assigned branch sees wasDelivered && qtyChanged (187, 195) and applies delta = new - stored (3-6 = -3, or 1-6 = -5) to inventory (196-200), clamped at 0 (85), writing no ledger row. 5) The tech's tilting count is now 3-5 below physical and nothing in bracket_usage_logs explains it.
findings.wrongBy: Tech shows (stored purchase qty - later-parsed qty) FEWER of that type than physical, on top of the owner's already-correct manual set; no ledger row
findings.structuralCause: The sync reconciles inventory against the purchase row's quantities, while a manual set reconciles inventory against physical stock; the two disagree about what the counter means and neither records the other. Precondition (a delivery email that parses a different qty than the confirmation) is plausible from the parser but not verifiable from code alone.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence (c722678 fixed a real 2/6/2-vs-1/3/1 over-parse on Jun 28, so over-credited deliveries have occurred)

findings.title: demo-seed.sql / demo-setup.sql delete the production businesses' inventory rows, and the Inventory tab silently re-creates zero rows so nothing looks missing
findings.scenario: 1) Someone pastes scripts/demo-seed.sql (or the 3766-line demo-setup.sql that embeds it) into the production project's SQL editor, trusting the '100% FICTIONAL' header. 2) Lines 275-278 run `delete from bracket_inventory ... where b.slug in ('handy-andy','doms')` -- the real production slugs (0030:34 seeds a real order under 'handy-andy'). Every real tech's running count is gone; no ledger row. 3) The fictional-name inserts at 289-308 match no real technician; the 'safety net' at 312-318 and the next Inventory tab view (admin.js 11852-11867 auto-inserts 0/0/0 for any active tech without a row) give every real tech a fresh zero row. 4) Every tech reads 0/0/0 with no error and no trace; the next job completions clamp at 0 (tech.js 1796-1798), so consumption is silently lost until someone re-counts every truck by hand.
findings.wrongBy: Every tech shows 0 of every type versus whatever they physically hold; subsequent deductions are clamped away until a manual re-count
findings.structuralCause: A seed script targets production business slugs with no project guard, and the read endpoint's auto-create side effect masks the destruction by manufacturing plausible zero rows.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: A physical recount is not a first-class event, so every later replay or backfill re-applies history the recount already absorbed
findings.scenario: 1) Jul 7: owner counts TK's and Greg's trucks and enters the physical numbers — either by pasting scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql into the Supabase SQL editor (absolute UPDATE, matches by name prefix, no ledger row) or via the Inventory tab 'Edit' → 'Set Brackets' modal (public/admin.html:11443-11466, prompt reads 'this replaces the current number'; no reason field, no 'counted on' date). The DB now holds a number with no marker that it is a physical baseline: bracket_inventory has only updated_at (0029:46-55) which every write bumps, and the ledger row for a UI set carries used-columns 0 with 'flat 5→10' only in free text (api/admin.js:12156-12171). 2) Sept 2: someone audits, finds 13 jobs completed before ba87325 that have no bracket_deducted_at stamp and no ledger row, and runs a retroactive decrement directly in Supabase (recorded only in the 3b1183a commit body). Nothing in the data says 'these July jobs were already netted out by the Jul 7 count', so the decrement is applied again. 3) TK, Greg, Juan, Steve now read lower than their trucks by the brackets those July jobs consumed. Only the owner's memory could have caught it; the code's only guard against re-deducting a job is the per-booking metadata stamp (api/admin.js:4349, api/tech.js:980), which pre-Jul-7 jobs never had.
findings.wrongBy: Each affected tech (TK, Greg, Juan, Steve) shows FEWER brackets than physical by the sum of bracket lines on their pre-2026-07-07 completed jobs that the Sept-2 backfill decremented (13 jobs total per 3b1183a); direction is always low, per tech, per type
findings.structuralCause: The counter is a mutable running number with no 'as counted at <time>' checkpoint and no typed ledger event for 'physical recount'. A manual set, a raw SQL reset, a delivery credit and a consumption all look identical to any later reconciliation (or are invisible to it), so nobody — human or script — can answer 'which jobs happened after the last count'. The Set modal and the SQL template both invite exactly this kind of unmarked overwrite.
findings.alreadyHappened: Yes — the 2026-09-03 incident: ba87325 (2026-07-07) shipped fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql as the Jul 7 physical reset; 3b1183a (2026-09-02) commit body records a direct-in-Supabase retroactive decrement of 13 pre-ba87325 jobs, which double-deducted TK/Greg/Juan/Steve. fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql:32-33 also references an earlier 'reset to 0' for Juan that exists nowhere in the repo.

findings.title: The ledger is write-only: nothing in either app or any report reads bracket_usage_logs, so clamp WARNINGs and 'needs manual attribution' rows never reach a human
findings.scenario: 1) A credit is lost for any reason (see HP-4) so TK's documented full-motion count is 0 while he physically has 5. 2) TK completes three full-motion jobs in the tech app. Each time api/tech.js:992 → adjustBracketInventory computes Math.max(0, 0-1) = 0 (tech.js:1796-1798); the count does not move; a ledger row is written with full_motion_used=1 and a '— WARNING: full_motion already below the deducted qty, decrement clamped at 0' note (tech.js:1810-1823). 3) No screen shows those rows: a repo-wide grep finds no .select on bracket_usage_logs in api/ or public/ — renderBrackets (public/admin.html:11078-11390) reads only bracket_inventory and purchases, the low-stock logic (11648-11663) reads only the counts, and there is no Supabase alert. 4) The owner sees '⚠ Reorder Full Motion' (11119-11121) and orders 5 more; on delivery the count becomes 5 while TK physically has 2+5=7. The three consumptions are permanently masked, and any future 'replay the ledger' reconciliation will subtract them a second time.
findings.wrongBy: After the sequence TK shows 5 full-motion vs 7 physical (2 LOW); a later ledger replay would move him to 2 (5 LOW). Each clamped completion silently widens the gap by that job's bracket qty and leaves the only evidence in an unread table
findings.structuralCause: The ledger was bolted on (7b166cb) as a best-effort side effect with the intent 'next drift = one SQL query', not as something a human sees. Clamp-at-zero converts a data error into silence: the counter refuses to go negative (which would be a visible, alarming signal) and the WARNING goes to a table with no reader, no badge, no notification. The same is true of the unattributed 'inventory NOT deducted, needs manual attribution' rows written at api/admin.js:4377-4382 — the office has no queue that lists them.
findings.alreadyHappened: Yes — 7b166cb (2026-08-21) commit body: 'TK's physical bracket count didn't match the documented count and there was no way to prove why ... the floor-at-zero clamp silently swallowed decrements whenever the documented count was already too low.' The fix added the WARNING rows but no reader; the Sept-2 audit (3b1183a) again had to be done by hand in Supabase.

findings.title: Office/secretary 'Mark complete' bypasses the two-tech supplier gate and always charges the primary tech; the dashboard has no supplier control and secretaries cannot see or fix inventory
findings.scenario: 1) Two-tech Dom's job: TK primary, Greg secondary. Greg pulls the tilting bracket from his own truck. 2) They leave without tapping Complete (or the app blocks them: 2-photo gate api/tech.js:40, 913-918, or the 'Select which technician supplied the bracket' gate at 923-928 / 1938-1951). 3) That evening Joey (secretary) opens the booking on the dashboard and clicks '✓ Mark complete' (public/admin.html:3314, 3386 — the confirm mentions only payment, never brackets). api/admin.js:340 accepts any admin token; bookingUpdate has no owner check; 4155 sets status=completed. 4) At 4357-4359 bracket_supplied_by is null so supplier = technician_id = TK → adjustBracketInventory(-1 tilting) against TK at 4362, and the ledger row says 'job completion (office)'. Greg is untouched. 5) The dashboard has no field to record or change the supplier (grep for bracket_supplied_by / job_bracket_supplier in public/admin.html: none); Joey cannot see the counts as anything but a static chip (11119-11121) and bracket_update is owner-only (12081). The only remedy is for a tech to reopen the completed job in the tech app and use 'Change' supplier (tech.js:1208-1240), which nobody is prompted to do.
findings.wrongBy: TK shows 1 tilting FEWER than physical; Greg shows 1 tilting MORE than physical (per bracket on every two-tech job completed from the dashboard without a recorded supplier)
findings.structuralCause: Two completion paths with different business rules: the tech app enforces 'who supplied it' before completion, the dashboard silently defaults to the primary tech. Permission split is inverted for the process: the role most likely to complete jobs after-hours (secretary) can move inventory but is read-only on the Inventory tab, while the only role that can correct it (owner) is not told a correction is needed.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence in git for the two-tech dashboard case specifically; 3b1183a (2026-09-02) confirms the dashboard completion path is used in practice and was found to be skipping bracket accounting silently on a related class of jobs

findings.title: Owner flips a Walmart order's dropdown to 'Delivered' on an auto-assigned order → the order is never credited, and no record exists that a credit was expected
findings.scenario: 1) A Walmart order ships to Juan's house; the email scanner auto-assigns it to Juan by street number + ZIP (api/migrate.js:113-120, 125-139) and creates an in_route row. 2) Juan texts 'brackets came' before Walmart's delivery email is parsed (or it never parses). The owner opens Inventory → Recent Walmart Orders and changes the status dropdown to '✓ Delivered' (public/admin.html:11318-11324 → setBracketStatus 11050-11056). 3) api/admin.js:12058-12076 bracketSetStatus updates only bracket_purchases.status/delivered_date — no inventory write, no ledger row. 4) Fifteen minutes later the cron POSTs the real delivery email: in bracketSync the row is already 'delivered' so wasDelivered=true and the credit at api/migrate.js:192-194 is skipped; qtys match so the heal at 195-200 is a no-op. bracketAssign (12583-12592) cannot help because the row is already assigned. 5) Juan physically has +15 brackets; the count did not move; 'Brackets In Route' stops listing the order so even the visual cue is gone. Mirror case: the owner picks the wrong row and flips a credited order back to 'In route' — the next scan sees !wasDelivered and credits the whole order a second time. The GitHub workflow's manual override (bracket-tracker.yml:39-56) has the identical effect: it posts status with no quantities, so totalQty=0 blocks the credit and sets the latch.
findings.wrongBy: Juan shows the full order quantity FEWER than physical (e.g. 5/5/5 = 15 brackets low) with no trace; the mirror flip shows the full order quantity MORE than physical
findings.structuralCause: The Walmart 'status' dropdown looks like a stock control to the owner but is only a label on the purchase row, while the sync treats that same label as its one-way idempotency latch. Because credits never write a ledger row and bracket_purchases has no 'credited' flag (only wire_plate_purchases got one in 0041), nothing can later show that a delivered order was never applied to a count.
findings.alreadyHappened: No direct evidence of the dropdown path; the same outcome (delivered order, count never credited) was repaired by raw SQL in 48c9475 fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql on 2026-07-07, which itself left no ledger row and is non-idempotent (+5/+5/+5 on every run).

findings.title: A tech editing line items on an already-completed job changes the ticket and payroll but never the count; the identical edit from the office does reconcile
findings.scenario: 1) Zach completes a job in the app with one 'Tilting (recommended)' line: api/tech.js:992 deducts 1 tilting and stamps bracket_deducted_at. 2) The customer had added a second TV on site; Zach forgot the line. Next morning he opens the completed job in the tech app — the Line Items editor and Save button are rendered on every job regardless of status (public/tech.html:1105-1109, 1391-1394) — adds 'Tilting bracket' ×1 and saves. 3) api/tech.js jobLineItemsSave (681+) has no status check and never calls adjustBracketInventory (its only callers in tech.js are 992, 1238, 1239). The ticket now says 2 brackets, payroll pays 2, the ledger says 1 used, the count moved 1. 4) Had Heather made the same edit from the dashboard, api/admin.js:4658-4671 would have restored 1 and charged 2. Nobody is told which path was used.
findings.wrongBy: Zach shows 1 tilting MORE than physical (the delta of bracket lines added after completion; removing a line the other way leaves him LOW)
findings.structuralCause: Bracket consumption is derived from free-text line-item names at one instant (completion) and the 'keep the count consistent with the ticket' rule was re-implemented per writer: it was added to the office save on 2026-09-02 and not to the tech save. There is no single 'ticket changed' hook, so each editing surface can silently disagree with the counter.
findings.alreadyHappened: No direct evidence for the tech side; 3b1183a (2026-09-02) found the office-side twin of this gap live ('bookingLineItemsSave never touched bracket accounting at all') and fixed only api/admin.js. Throckmorton (1959e92, 2026-08-21) shows tech and office both editing tickets after the fact in practice.

findings.title: The Set Brackets modal is prefilled from a stale screen and overwrites all three counts, silently erasing any automatic deduction since the page was drawn — and the ledger row makes it look intentional
findings.scenario: 1) 8:00 the owner opens the Inventory tab. renderBrackets runs only on navigation or after an action (public/admin.html:2443, 2470, 11054, 11487...) — there is no timer for this tab — and bakes TK's numbers 5/3/2 into the Edit button's onclick (11129). 2) 11:00 TK completes a flat-bracket job: count becomes 4/3/2, ledger 'auto-deduct'. 3) 14:00 the owner, still on the 8:00 screen, hands TK two tilting brackets from the garage and records it the only way possible: Edit → modal prefilled 5/3/2 (11447-11456) → changes Tilting to 5 → Save (11470-11482 posts flat 5, tilting 5, full_motion 2, action 'set'). 4) api/admin.js:12115-12118 accepts the absolute values and 12140-12149 writes all three columns: flat is back to 5 while TK's truck has 4. 5) The ledger row (12165-12169) reads 'manual set by office: flat 4→5, tilting 3→5' — indistinguishable from a deliberate correction, and the hand delivery of 2 tilting is recorded as a 'set' rather than a receipt.
findings.wrongBy: TK shows 1 flat MORE than physical; more generally every automatic movement between page render and Save is reverted, in either direction
findings.structuralCause: There is no 'brackets received by hand' or 'transfer between techs' event, so the absolute-overwrite Set modal doubles as receiving, transfer and recount. An absolute set from a client-side snapshot is last-writer-wins against the automatic paths, and the ledger records the outcome as if the owner chose it.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: A job completed by mistake and then reopened + cancelled (or reassigned) keeps its deduction forever; nothing restores it and nobody is prompted
findings.scenario: 1) Heather has two same-day bookings for customers named Johnson; she clicks '✓ Mark complete' on the wrong one from the dashboard (public/admin.html:3314, 3386; no photo/payment gate on this path). api/admin.js:4155 → 4362 deducts 1 full-motion from the assigned tech Steve and stamps bracket_deducted_at. 2) She notices and clicks 'Reopen job' (3315; canReopen 3206) — api/admin.js:4129-4143 spreads existing.metadata into the patch, so the stamp survives. 3) The customer then cancels: 'Cancel' → 4011-4015 sets status=cancelled. No branch in either file ever restores a deduction on cancel/no_show — the only +1 calls in the codebase are the office line-item edit (api/admin.js:4670) and the tech supplier change (api/tech.js:1238). 4) Steve's bracket is still in his truck; his count is 1 low; the ledger shows an 'auto-deduct (job completion (office))' row attached to a booking whose status is 'cancelled', which no screen surfaces. Variant: instead of cancelling, Heather reassigns the reopened job to Juan who does it a week later — the stamp still blocks a second deduction (4349), so Steve stays 1 low and Juan is 1 high, with no ledger row for Juan at all.
findings.wrongBy: Steve shows 1 full-motion FEWER than physical (cancel variant); in the reassign variant Steve is 1 low and Juan 1 high
findings.structuralCause: The deduction is bound to 'status became completed' but not to 'status stopped being completed'. Reopen deliberately preserves the stamp to prevent double-deduction, which makes it impossible for a later cancel, no-show or reassignment to know the deduction should be reversed or moved. There is no compensating event type in the ledger for 'returned to truck'.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Office completes a booking that has no technician assigned: consumption is logged 'needs manual attribution' to a table nobody reads and the count never moves, even after the tech is later assigned
findings.scenario: 1) A walk-in / imported Houston job is done by Juan but technician_id was never set in the system (the office assigns it later for payroll). 2) Heather clicks '✓ Mark complete' on the dashboard. api/admin.js:4357-4359 finds no bracket_supplied_by and no technician_id, so the else-branch at 4367-4384 inserts a bracket_usage_logs row with technician_id=null and notes 'inventory NOT deducted, needs manual attribution', and deliberately does not stamp bracket_deducted_at. 3) Nothing lists that row (no reader of bracket_usage_logs anywhere in api/ or public/), so no one knows attribution is pending. 4) Heather later assigns Juan via the booking's assign action (4124-4127) — that does not re-run the deduction. The 'Mark complete' button is hidden once status is completed (canAssign, public/admin.html:3205), and the office line-item reconcile (4658) is gated on the very stamp that was left unset, so neither everyday action will ever deduct it. Juan's count stays high by the job's brackets unless someone knows to Reopen and re-complete.
findings.wrongBy: Juan shows the job's bracket lines MORE than physical (e.g. +1 full-motion per such job), permanently, with the only evidence in an unread ledger row
findings.structuralCause: The fix for 'silently skipped' was 'log it and hope' — a pending-attribution state with no queue, no badge and no owner-facing action to resolve it. The dashboard workflow (complete first, assign tech later for payroll) is exactly the order that triggers it.
findings.alreadyHappened: Partially — 3b1183a (2026-09-02) found this office path skipping bracket accounting entirely while auditing Juan's count; the fix converts the silent skip into an unread row, so the count outcome is unchanged.

findings.title: Assigning an in-route Walmart order from the other company's tab makes the delivery credit land on a phantom (wrong-business, tech) row; the tech's real stock never goes up and the next job clamps it at 0
findings.scenario:
1. Cron mirrors Walmart order X (5 full_motion, unknown address) as an unassigned in_route row in BOTH businesses (api/migrate.js:248-274).
2. Owner has the Dom's tab loaded, opens Inventory, and in 'Unassigned Walmart Orders' picks Steve (a Handy Andy tech) — the picker now lists every business's techs (public/admin.html:11088, 11357; enabled by commit 3f80949, 2026-09-02).
3. bracketAssign loads the DOM'S copy of the row (.eq('business_id', bizId), api/admin.js:12540), looks Steve up with no business filter (:12551), stamps technician_id=Steve on that Dom's row (:12567), deletes the Handy Andy unassigned twin (:12580), and because status is in_route it credits nothing (:12587).
4. Fifteen minutes to a week later the delivery email arrives; bracketSync finds assignedRow = the Dom's row (api/migrate.js:177), sees in_route->delivered, and calls adjustBracketInventory(db, assignedRow.business_id /* Dom's */, Steve, {full_motion:5}) (:193). No (Dom's, Steve) row exists, so :89-93 INSERTS one with full_motion_qty=5. Steve's real (Handy Andy, Steve) row is untouched.
5. Steve uses one on a job and taps Complete; tech.js adjustBracketInventory resolves his HOME business (api/tech.js:1789-1793) and decrements the Handy Andy row, which never got the 5 — Math.max(0, ...) at :1796-1798 swallows it and the ledger only gets a WARNING string (:1822).
6. Every later scan with a qty correction self-heals the phantom row again (api/migrate.js:196), never the real one. The tech app shows Steve his Handy Andy row (api/tech.js:2497-2502) and an 'on the way' list filtered to auth.business_id (:2522-2527), so he sees neither the in-route order nor the credit.
findings.wrongBy: Steve's real row shows 5 fewer full_motion than physical (and a further -1 per job that clamped at 0); a second bracket_inventory row (Dom's, Steve) shows +5 that no deduction path will ever touch, so the Inventory tab's per-tech total across both rows overstates by the clamped jobs and understates on the row the office actually edits.
findings.structuralCause: bracket_purchases rows are keyed per business (mirrored twins) but the tech is a single person with one truck stock; bracketAssign stamps the tech onto whichever business's copy was loaded, and the sync's copy of adjustBracketInventory (migrate.js) keys the stock row by the PURCHASE ROW's business instead of resolving technicians.business_id. The July-16 home-business fix (5199678) was applied to the admin.js and tech.js copies only — `git log -S homeBizId` never touches api/migrate.js — and 3f80949 (Sept 2) opened cross-tab assignment without revisiting the sync side.
findings.alreadyHappened: Same failure class already occurred: commit 5199678 (2026-07-16) — completing TK's cross-hire Handy Andy job created a phantom always-zero (handy-andy, TK) bracket_inventory row that showed a false reorder alert; it was deleted by hand in Supabase with no ledger row. This exact assign-then-deliver path only became reachable with 3f80949 (2026-09-02 23:30), so no evidence yet of a second occurrence.

findings.title: Inventory tab renders every bracket_inventory row (so a tech with a phantom row appears twice), but Edit/Reorder on the phantom row silently writes the tech's HOME row — the owner 'corrects' a number they are not looking at, and nothing in the app can zero or delete the phantom
findings.scenario:
1. Start from any phantom-row state (CBI-1, or the July-16 TK case): Steve has (handy-andy, Steve) = 3/2/0 and (doms, Steve) = 0/0/5.
2. Owner opens Inventory. bracketInventory reads across all businesses and returns BOTH rows (api/admin.js:11829-11833, `final` concatenates every inv row at :11870, tagged with its business at :11903). The table shows 'Steve [Handy Andy] 3/2/0 ⚠ Reorder Full Motion' and 'Steve [Dom's] 0/0/5 ⚠ Reorder Flat, Tilting'.
3. Owner clicks Edit on the Dom's line. openBracketEdit is prefilled from THAT row's numbers 0/0/5 (public/admin.html:11129, :11443-11455). Owner reasons 'he has the 5 FM from the order plus his 3 flat / 2 tilting' and types 3/2/5, Save.
4. saveBracketCount posts action:'set' with only technician_id (public/admin.html:11470-11490); bracketUpdate ignores the loaded tab and resolves technicians.business_id (api/admin.js:12094-12096), overwriting the HANDY ANDY row to 3/2/5 (:12147-12148). The Dom's phantom stays 0/0/5.
5. The table now shows 3/2/5 and 0/0/5 for the same person: full_motion is counted twice (physical: 5). lowStockCount (public/admin.html:11698, used at :11740) still counts the phantom as a low-stock tech and the '⚠ Reorder Flat, Tilting' chip stays on forever; the only removal path is raw SQL (as 5199678 did).
6. Side effect of the same keying: bracketInventory's auto-create keys `invByTech` by technician_id only (api/admin.js:11856-11857), so a tech whose ONLY row is a phantom never gets a home row created by the page — it is created by the first job completion with a clamped 0 (api/tech.js:1796-1801).
findings.wrongBy: The dashboard shows the tech's stock split across two rows whose sum overstates physical by the phantom's contents (here +5 full_motion), while the home row — the only one the office can edit and the only one deductions touch — was just overwritten with whatever the owner typed while reading the phantom; the low-stock counter over-reports by one tech per phantom row.
findings.structuralCause: unique(business_id, technician_id) (0029:54) permits N rows per tech; the read path shows all N, the write path always targets exactly one (home business), and no endpoint exposes the row id. A phantom row is therefore visible, alarming, and unreachable from the UI.
findings.alreadyHappened: Commit 5199678 (2026-07-16): the phantom (handy-andy, TK) row produced a false 'reorder' alert on the Handy Andy inventory table and had to be 'cleaned up directly in the database' — the no-UI-removal half of this finding is confirmed; the mis-targeted Edit half has no evidence.

findings.title: Office 'Mark complete' on a cross-company two-tech job charges the primary tech's company stock even when the partner-company helper supplied the bracket (no supplier gate on the office path)
findings.scenario:
1. Dom's books a large-TV job with TK (Dom's) as primary and, via the cross-company pool, Steve (Handy Andy) as secondary (api/admin.js:109, :2565, :5899). Line items include 1 full_motion bracket.
2. On site, Steve supplies the bracket from his truck. Nobody records it: the tech app only asks 'who supplied the bracket' on the job card and gates the tech-side Complete button (api/tech.js:925-927 -> jobNeedsBracketSupplier :1938-1951), but the techs leave without tapping Complete.
3. The office marks the job complete from the dashboard. admin.js bookingUpdate has NO jobNeedsBracketSupplier check (grep: the only bracket_supplied_by reads are :4331, :4358, :4403, :4666); supplier resolves to bracket_supplied_by || technician_id || existing.technician_id = TK (:4359) and adjustBracketInventory(-1) debits TK's Dom's row (:4362), stamping bracket_deducted_at (:4364-4366).
4. Steve's Handy Andy row is untouched. Nothing later re-attributes it: reopen->recomplete keeps the stamp, and the line-item reconcile (:4658-4679) uses the same TK fallback (:4667). Only if a tech later opens the completed job in the tech app and uses 'Change' on the bracket card (api/tech.js:1236-1240) does the +1/-1 move happen.
findings.wrongBy: TK shows 1 fewer full_motion than physical; Steve shows 1 more — the deficit sits on the wrong company's stock until someone notices, and the ledger row (logged under TK's home business, api/admin.js:12297) attributes consumption to the wrong tech.
findings.structuralCause: bracket_supplied_by is optional data that only the tech app collects and only enforces on tech-side completion; every office-side writer (completion, line-item reconcile) falls back to the primary technician, which on a cross-hire job is by construction the tech from the OTHER company than the helper.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Name-prefix technician lookups with no active/ORDER BY guard (sync auto-assign, raw fix scripts) can credit a different technician row than the real one, creating an inventory row under a placeholder identity
findings.scenario:
1. The July Zenbooker history import created ~20 inactive placeholder technicians in Handy Andy (api/admin.js:10440-10443 inserts active:false rows named from body.crew_names; commit 5bcdad1 describes them). Any future re-import with a crew name typed as e.g. 'Juan (2023)' or 'Steve B' creates a second row whose name starts with the real tech's first name.
2. A Walmart delivery email for Juan's home address arrives. matchTechByAddress selects `.eq('business_id', HA).ilike('name','juan%').limit(1)` with no active filter and no ORDER BY (api/migrate.js:135-137); Postgres returns whichever row it likes — the placeholder.
3. bracketSync's matched branch stamps the placeholder's id on the purchase row (:225-233) and, because the email says delivered, credits (HA, placeholder) via adjustBracketInventory (:240), inserting a new bracket_inventory row (:89-93). Real Juan's row never moves; the Inventory tab now shows a 'Juan (2023)' line holding his brackets (api/admin.js:11829-11833 does not filter inactive techs' rows).
4. Same shape in the raw scripts already committed: scripts/fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql:34-41 inserts +5/+5/+5 for EVERY technicians row matching `name ilike 'juan%'` across ALL businesses (no business_id, no active filter); scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql:14-25 resets every `ilike 'tk%'` / `'greg%'` row in any business. One extra name match = one extra credited/reset row, with no ledger trace.
findings.wrongBy: Real tech's count is short by the whole delivery (e.g. Juan -5/-5/-5) while a placeholder/duplicate identity row carries the credit; for the raw scripts, an extra matching row gets a full duplicate +5/+5/+5 or a baseline reset it was never counted for.
findings.structuralCause: Technician identity is resolved by free-text name prefix (hardcoded TECH_HOME_ADDRESSES names, ilike in SQL) rather than by technician id, in a technicians table that now contains inactive placeholder rows and can contain same-prefix names across businesses; inventory rows are then keyed to whichever row matched.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence — the import attaches the known names 'Juan'/'Zach' to existing rows (api/admin.js:10430-10432), and the seeded roster (0001:491-500) has no duplicate prefixes today.

findings.title: Ledger rows are keyed to different businesses depending on the helper (bracket rows under the tech's home business, wire-plate/Apple-TV and unattributed rows under the job's business), so any per-business or per-row reconstruction of a cross-hire tech's count mis-buckets
findings.scenario:
1. TK (Dom's) completes a Handy Andy cross-hire job that used 1 tilting bracket and 1 wire plate.
2. adjustBracketInventory writes the bracket ledger row with business_id = homeBizId = Dom's (api/tech.js:1818; api/admin.js:12297). adjustWirePlateInventory writes the plate row with business_id = the JOB's business = Handy Andy (api/tech.js:1882; api/admin.js:12335), and adjustAppleTvBracketInventory likewise (api/tech.js:1928; api/admin.js:12382). The office no-supplier branch writes technician_id=null under the job's business (api/admin.js:4377-4382). Manual set/adjust rows go under the home business (api/admin.js:12165-12169).
3. The stock row itself is always the home-business row (api/tech.js:1789-1793). Anyone later reconstructing TK's Dom's row from bracket_usage_logs filtered by business_id=Dom's (the natural query, and the one the commit 5199678 message tells you is correct: 'usage logs still attribute to the job's business') gets the bracket deductions but not the plate deductions, or vice versa; a query by job business misses the bracket rows entirely. This is the exact class of blind spot that let the Sept-2 backfill re-deduct July jobs.
findings.wrongBy: Not a live count error; a reconstruction of a cross-hire tech's home-business row from the ledger is off by every cross-hire plate/Apple-TV deduction (filtered by home business) or by every cross-hire bracket deduction (filtered by job business).
findings.structuralCause: Commit 5199678 (2026-07-16) deliberately kept usage logs on the job's business while moving stock rows to the home business; commit 7b166cb (2026-08-21) then added the bracket ledger insert keyed on homeBizId, leaving the plate/Apple-TV inserts on the job business. Three copies of the convention now disagree and no consumer normalises them.
findings.alreadyHappened: Indirect: the 2026-09-03 incident (Sept-2 backfill re-deducting July jobs already absorbed by the Jul-7 raw reset) is the same failure mode — the ledger could not be trusted as a per-tech record — though that instance was caused by missing rows rather than mis-keyed ones.

findings.title: Raw-SQL physical reset (Jul 7) followed by a raw-SQL retroactive backfill (Sep 2) re-debits jobs the reset already absorbed
findings.scenario: 1) Jun 25-Jul 7: TK/Greg/Juan/Steve complete solo jobs; the app deducts nothing (solo auto-decrement did not exist before ba87325) and writes no bracket_deducted_at stamp. 2) Jul 7: owner pastes scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql into the Supabase SQL editor: `update app.bracket_inventory set full_motion_qty = 1 ... where t.name ilike 'tk%'` and `set full_motion_qty = 3, flat_qty = 2, tilting_qty = 2 ... ilike 'greg%'` -- an absolute SET to the counted truck stock, which by definition already reflects every bracket consumed on those June/July jobs; no bracket_usage_logs row, no marker on bracket_inventory or on the bookings. (Same commit ba87325 turned on auto-decrement; scripts/fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql from 48c9475 says Juan 'was reset to 0 earlier', another unrecorded reset.) 3) Sep 2: an audit run directly in Supabase (commit 3b1183a message: 'the other 13, from before solo-job auto-decrement existed (commit ba87325), got their real decrement applied retroactively') selects completed bookings with bracket lines and no bracket_deducted_at and subtracts their quantities from bracket_inventory. Nothing in the DB or code tells the backfill that a physical count taken AFTER those jobs already absorbed them, so each of those jobs is now debited a second time. 4) Residual: if that direct-SQL backfill did not also write bracket_deducted_at, those 13 jobs still have no stamp, so any later office Reopen -> Mark complete (admin.js:4129-4143 keeps metadata, 4349 checks only the stamp) debits them a THIRD time. The same applies to any Jun 25-Jul 7 two-tech job whose supplier was recorded: the pre-ba87325 jobBracketSetSupplier deducted immediately with no stamp (ba87325 diff removed `if (prev) await adjustBracketInventory(..., +1); await adjustBracketInventory(..., supplierId, qtys, -1);` with no metadata write), so a no-stamp-based backfill re-deducts those too.
findings.wrongBy: Each affected tech shows FEWER brackets than physical by the sum of every pre-Jul-7 job the backfill replayed (TK/Greg/Juan/Steve, per the 2026-09-03 incident); a later reopen->recomplete of any unstamped backfilled job subtracts the same job's brackets again.
codeRefs: git 3b1183a (commit body: backfill done directly in Supabase)
git ba87325 (ships the reset script and the stamp in the same commit; removed the unstamped supplier-picker deduction in api/tech.js)
findings.structuralCause: bracket_inventory is a bare mutable counter with no record of WHEN it was last reconciled to physical stock, and raw SQL writes it with no ledger row or marker. The only idempotency memory the system has is bookings.metadata.bracket_deducted_at, which a physical reset does not set and a raw backfill cannot consult. Any replay keyed on 'completed and unstamped' therefore re-applies consumption that a later physical count already includes.
findings.alreadyHappened: YES -- this is the 2026-09-03 incident (double-deduction for TK, Greg, Juan, Steve). git: ba87325 2026-07-07 adds scripts/fix-bracket-inventory-baseline.sql; 3b1183a 2026-09-02 commit body documents the direct-Supabase backfill of 13 pre-ba87325 jobs.

findings.title: Two-tech job completed from the office dashboard, then a tech records the bracket supplier: second deduction with no restore
findings.scenario: 1) A two-tech job (technician_id = A, secondary_technician_id = B) carries a company bracket line; nobody has recorded bracket_supplied_by. 2) Office clicks 'Mark complete' (admin.html:3314/3386 -> booking_update action=status completed). The office path has NO jobNeedsBracketSupplier gate (admin.js:4318-4390; the gate exists only in the tech path, tech.js:925-927), so it resolves supplier = bracket_supplied_by || technician_id = A (admin.js:4357-4359) and calls adjustBracketInventory(A, -1) then stamps bracket_deducted_at (4362-4366). A's count -1. 3) That evening B (who actually brought the bracket) opens the completed job in the tech app: the day list shows completed jobs (tech.html:533 'Completed ✓' badge, 1004/1015 open showDetail) and the bracket card is rendered whenever j.bracket.needed (tech.html:1127-1141), which tech.js:489-506 sets true for any job with secondary_technician_id and bracket lines regardless of status; supplied_by is null so it shows 'Who supplied this bracket? Required before completing.' with the select. 4) B picks B -> job_bracket_supplier -> jobBracketSetSupplier: prev = b.bracket_supplied_by = null (tech.js:1230), metadata.bracket_deducted_at is set (1237), so `if (prev)` at 1238 is skipped and 1239 runs adjustBracketInventory(B, -1). B's count -1. Now A -1 AND B -1 for one physical bracket. Variant: B picks A instead (the tech the office already charged): prev (null) !== A so the early return at 1231 does not fire, 1238 is skipped, 1239 charges A AGAIN -> A -2.
findings.wrongBy: One bracket of the job's type is debited from two techs (A and B each -1), or twice from A (-2) if the picker is set to the tech the office already charged; physical stock moved by 1.
findings.structuralCause: Two writers implement the completion protocol independently: the office path charges the primary tech as a fallback without recording bracket_supplied_by, while the tech supplier picker assumes 'no bracket_supplied_by' means 'nobody has been charged yet' and only restores a tech named in that column. The stamp records THAT a deduction happened but not WHO was charged, so the second writer cannot reverse the first.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence in git (two-tech jobs are live: 61f8fe6 2026-07-17 'TK/Juan split normally when a real second tech is assigned'; office completion of two-tech jobs with no supplier is exactly the 'no supplier on file' case 3b1183a found in the audit)
