findings.title: Estimate bracket-upgrade upsell persists as a second bracket line; completion debits N+1 brackets for N TVs
findings.scenario: 1) Office builds a New Booking/estimate for 1 TV with base bracket 'Flat'. nbBracketUpsell (admin.html:16552-16572) offers 'Upgrade to a Tilting Bracket' priced at the delta; NB_BASE_PRESENCE (16522-16529) has no bracket entry, so the base 'Flat' selection stays in the quote. 2) Customer approves and accepts the upgrade: estimateApprove builds `combined = baseItems.concat(upsellsAsLineItems(accepted))` (admin.js:10912) and bookEstimateAppointment inserts every combined item as a booking_line_items row with name = description (10798-10804). The ticket now carries BOTH 'Flat' (qty 1) and 'Upgrade to a Tilting Bracket' (qty 1). 3) Tech (or office) completes the job. detectBracketQtys (tech.js:1753-1761 / admin.js:12242-12250) counts flat += 1 from 'flat' and tilting += 1 from 'upgrade to a tilting bracket' (/tilt/). 4) clampBracketQtysToTvCount sees total 2 > 1 TV but only trims when ONE category has >= 2 lines with a non-selection label (line-items.js:184-190); here flat has 1 line and tilting has 1 line, so it logs 'NOT clamping' and stands down. adjustBracketInventory(-1) removes 1 flat AND 1 tilting from the supplier. Physically the tech installed one tilting bracket. Same shape for 'Tilting (recommended)' + 'Upgrade to a Full-Motion Bracket' (tilting +N, full_motion +1).
findings.wrongBy: Supplier tech shows 1 fewer FLAT (or tilting, for the full-motion upgrade) than physical on every estimate-booked job where the customer accepted the bracket upgrade; the upgraded TV's bracket is debited once as the base type and once as the upgrade type.
findings.structuralCause: Bracket consumption is derived by regex over free-text line-item names rather than a structured per-TV bracket field, and the upsell model expresses an UPGRADE as an additive line next to the base line instead of replacing it. The TV-count clamp was tuned to the Throckmorton shape (two lines in one category) and deliberately declines to trim cross-category overcounts.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence (no DB access taken; the upsell code path has existed since the estimate upsell feature and is exercised on every approved estimate with an accepted bracket upgrade)

findings.title: Reopen -> reassign -> recomplete -> line-item edit debits the consumed bracket from the new tech while the old tech's debit is never restored
findings.scenario: 1) Office had A assigned; B actually did the job and installed a full-motion bracket, but the ticket says 'Tilting (recommended)'. Office clicks 'Mark complete' (admin.html:3386): supplier = technician_id = A (admin.js:4359), A tilting -1, stamp written (4362-4366). 2) Next day, for payroll, office clicks 'Reopen job' (admin.html:3387 -> admin.js:4129-4143): status -> assigned, patch.metadata spreads existing.metadata so bracket_deducted_at SURVIVES. 3) canAssign is now true (admin.html:3205), office picks B in the Assign dropdown (3367 -> assign branch admin.js:4095-4125, no bracket logic), then 'Mark complete' again: 4349 sees the stamp and skips the deduction. Counts: A tilting -1, B unchanged. 4) Office fixes the ticket (booking_line_items_save) from tilting to full motion: bookingLineItemsSave sees the stamp (4658), qtys differ (4661), resolves supplier FRESH as bracket_supplied_by || technician_id = B (4665-4667), and runs adjustBracketInventory(B, oldQtys, +1) then (B, newQtys, -1) (4670-4671). Final: A tilting -1 (A used nothing), B tilting +1 (phantom credit), B full_motion -1. The tilting bracket was debited from A and 'restored' to B; the ledger shows a normal-looking restore/deduct pair on B and a normal-looking deduct on A.
findings.wrongBy: A shows 1 fewer tilting than physical; B shows 1 more tilting than physical (B's full_motion -1 is correct). Net across the fleet the tilting count is right but each truck is wrong by one in opposite directions, so the low-stock alert fires for the wrong tech.
findings.structuralCause: The stamp records that a deduction happened but not which technician was charged or for what quantities; every later reconciler (line-item edit, supplier picker) re-derives the supplier from the CURRENT booking columns and reverses against that tech, so any reassignment between the original deduction and the reconcile silently moves stock between trucks.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence in git; the reconcile path is 1 day old (3b1183a 2026-09-02) and reassignment-after-completion is a real office workflow (61f8fe6 payroll tech-split fixes)

findings.title: Office and tech complete the same job within the same second (or office double-clicks): both pass the stamp check and both deduct
findings.scenario: 1) Job is in_progress. The office booking modal shows 'Mark complete' (canAssign true for non-terminal statuses, admin.html:3205, 3314) and the tech app shows 'Mark Complete' (tech.html:1026-1028). 2) Office clicks it and confirms while the tech taps completeYes (tech.html:2633-2637). 3) Tech handler reads existing at tech.js:892 (status in_progress, no stamp) and passes TERMINAL_STATUS (895) and the same-status replay guard (906); office handler reads existing at admin.js:3994 (same). 4) Both update bookings.status with no compare-and-swap on the prior status (tech.js:938 `.eq('id', id)`; admin.js:4245 `.eq('id', id).eq('business_id', ...)`). 5) Both evaluate `!existing.metadata?.bracket_deducted_at` against their own stale read (tech.js:980, admin.js:4349) and both call adjustBracketInventory, itself a JS select-then-update (tech.js:1791-1801, admin.js:12273-12283). Either both decrements land (-2) or the second read-modify-write overwrites the first (-1, then the two ledger rows say -2). Each then writes its own stamp (~8 round trips after its read). Variant without the tech: the office button is never disabled and updateBooking has no in-flight guard (admin.html:3386, 4073-4076); on a slow connection a second click+confirm while the first POST is in flight produces the same two unguarded requests.
findings.wrongBy: Supplier tech shows 1x the job's bracket quantity fewer than physical (both writers subtract), with two 'auto-deduct' ledger rows for the same booking_id.
findings.structuralCause: Idempotency is a check-then-act on a JSONB stamp read at handler start and written after ~8 more round trips; there is no atomic `UPDATE bookings SET status='completed' WHERE status <> 'completed'` claim, no unique index on bracket_usage_logs(booking_id, reason), and the inventory adjust is a non-atomic read-modify-write.
findings.alreadyHappened: no direct evidence for brackets; the same office+tech concurrency on one booking already produced a double CHARGE (git f72b66f 2026-07-16 'compare-and-swap lock so office + tech can't double-charge the same booking'), and no equivalent lock was added to completion.

findings.title: Office reassign/reschedule racing a tech completion overwrites the whole metadata blob and erases bracket_deducted_at; the next recomplete deducts again
findings.scenario: 1) Tech taps Mark Complete: tech.js:938 sets status completed, 992 deducts the supplier's brackets, then 994-997 re-reads metadata and writes bracket_deducted_at. 2) In the same window the office changes the 2nd tech or the primary on that job (admin.html:3367/3372 -> booking_update action=assign) or reschedules it. bookingUpdate read `existing` (including metadata) at admin.js:3994-3995, builds patch.metadata = { ...restMeta, reassigned_at } from that stale object (4118-4124; reschedule does the same at 4083-4085), then spends 11 awaits in the double-booking/availability guard (4164-4240) before `.update(patch)` at 4245. 3) The tech's stamp lands during those 11 awaits; the office's whole-object metadata write then replaces it with a copy that has no bracket_deducted_at (the pattern api/_lib/line-items.js:214-218 documents as a known residual). Status stays completed (office patch does not touch it), stock is already -1, stamp gone. 4) Days later the office clicks 'Reopen job' then 'Mark complete' (admin.html:3387, 3386): 4349 finds no stamp and deducts again -- from whichever tech is now technician_id (4359), which after the reassign may be a different tech than the one debited in step 1.
findings.wrongBy: Original supplier -1 (correct) plus the newly assigned tech -1 (phantom): fleet count is one job's bracket quantity lower than physical, split across two trucks.
findings.structuralCause: The only idempotency key for bracket deduction lives inside a single JSONB column that several unrelated handlers rewrite whole (last-writer-wins) from a read taken many round trips earlier. A lost stamp is indistinguishable from 'never deducted'.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence; the code comment at api/_lib/line-items.js:214-218 and the seal-fix comment at api/admin.js:4691-4694 acknowledge this exact clobber class was hit for li_rev and completion stamps, but only the line-item save paths were fixed.

findings.title: Any job deducted before the stamp existed is re-deducted on Reopen -> Mark complete
findings.scenario: 1) Between Jun 25 (dee47b2) and Jul 7 (ba87325), a two-tech job's supplier is recorded in the tech app: the old jobBracketSetSupplier called adjustBracketInventory(supplierId, qtys, -1) immediately and wrote no metadata stamp (ba87325 diff shows the removed lines `if (prev) await adjustBracketInventory(db, b.business_id, prev, qtys, +1); await adjustBracketInventory(db, b.business_id, supplierId, qtys, -1);` with no bookings.metadata write). Likewise, jobs the Sep-2 direct-SQL backfill decremented remain unstamped unless that SQL also set bracket_deducted_at (3b1183a body does not say it did). 2) Today the office opens one of those completed jobs (e.g. to fix the tech for payroll or the price): 'Reopen job' (admin.html:3387 -> admin.js:4129-4143, status assigned, metadata carried over -- still no stamp), then 'Mark complete' (3386). 3) admin.js:4349 `!existing.metadata?.bracket_deducted_at` is true, detectBracketQtys re-reads the ticket, adjustBracketInventory(-1) runs against bracket_supplied_by || technician_id (4359) and the stamp is written. The bracket was already subtracted in June (or on Sep 2).
findings.wrongBy: Supplier tech shows the job's bracket quantity fewer than physical, once more per reopen/recomplete of an unstamped-but-already-deducted job; for TK/Greg this stacks on top of DD-1 because the Jul-7 reset already absorbed the June consumption.
codeRefs: git ba87325 (api/tech.js diff, removed unstamped deduction in jobBracketSetSupplier)
git 3b1183a (backfill applied directly in Supabase, stamping not mentioned)
findings.structuralCause: The stamp was introduced after deductions had already been made by an earlier code path and by raw SQL, and no backfill ever wrote bracket_deducted_at for those. The completion guard treats 'no stamp' as 'never deducted', so every historical deduction that predates the stamp is re-armed.
findings.alreadyHappened: partial: the Sep-2 backfill itself selected jobs by the absence of the stamp and thereby re-deducted jobs the Jul-7 reset had absorbed (2026-09-03 incident); no evidence yet of a reopen->recomplete on a pre-stamp job.

findings.title: Bracket added after a zero-bracket completion is never debited (stamp-gated reconcile never arms)
findings.scenario: 1. Customer books online with 'I have my own bracket' (widget option, public/widget-dev.js:182), so the ticket has no flat/tilt/full-motion line. 2. On site the customer's bracket doesn't fit; the tech installs a company Tilting bracket from his truck. 3. Tech taps Complete in the app. detectBracketQtys returns 0, so tech.js skips the whole block at 985 — no deduction AND no bracket_deducted_at stamp (the stamp write at 996 is inside the `if (bracketTotal(need) > 0)` block). Same on the office path: admin.js 4354/4365. 4. Office is told 'we supplied a tilting' and edits the ticket in the dashboard, adding 'Tilting (recommended)' $60 (admin.html bkLiSave 3720 -> booking_line_items_save). 5. bookingLineItemsSave runs the bracket reconcile only `if (existing.metadata?.bracket_deducted_at)` (admin.js 4658) — the stamp was never written, so the +old/-new adjust at 4670-4671 is skipped silently. 6. Nothing ever revisits this job: reopen->recomplete would deduct (stamp unset, need now 1) but nobody is told to do it.
findings.wrongBy: Tech's tilting_qty shows +1 vs physical for every job of this shape (N brackets added after a bracket-less completion are never debited; ledger has no row either).
findings.structuralCause: bracket_deducted_at is overloaded as both 'already deducted' guard and 'this ticket's bracket accounting is live' flag, but it is only set when the FIRST completion found brackets. The reconcile added 2026-09-02 keys on the stamp instead of on bookings.status === 'completed', so a completed ticket that started at zero brackets can never enter reconciliation.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence — the reconcile path itself only exists since 3b1183a (2026-09-02) and was written with this stamp guard

findings.title: Tech-app line-item edit on a completed job never touches inventory (only the office editor reconciles)
findings.scenario: 1. Tech completes a 2-TV job whose ticket carried 1x 'Tilting (recommended)'; tech.js 992 deducts 1 tilting and stamps bracket_deducted_at at 996. 2. Later that day the tech remembers he also put a company Full Motion on the second TV and adds a 'Full Motion' $110 line (or bumps the tilting stepper 1->2) in the tech app Line Items card — the card and Save are mounted unconditionally (tech.html 1105-1109, mountTechLineItems at 1238), and jobLineItemsSave (tech.js 681-875) has no status check. 3. jobLineItemsSave replaces the rows, recomputes tax/price, bumps li_rev — and contains zero bracket code (no detectBracketQtys, no adjustBracketInventory anywhere between 681 and 875). 4. Variant: office reopens the job (admin.js 4129-4143 spreads existing.metadata so the stamp survives), tech edits as above, tech re-completes — tech.js 980 sees bracket_deducted_at already set and skips. Either way the added full_motion is never debited. Same hole for Apple TV brackets: neither editor reconciles appletv_bracket_deducted_at (admin.js 4394-4411 / tech.js 1007-1024 are completion-only).
findings.wrongBy: Supplier's count shows +1 per bracket line added/raised by a tech after completion (full_motion +1 in the example); ledger shows only the original deduction.
findings.structuralCause: The 2026-09-02 fix (3b1183a) put line-item->inventory reconciliation in admin.js bookingLineItemsSave only; the tech.js editor, which the ledger-less Throckmorton incident proved is used on live tickets, was not given the same code. Consumption is derived from line items, but only one of the two line-item writers re-derives it.
findings.alreadyHappened: no direct evidence of a post-completion tech edit; Throckmorton (2026-08-21, commit 1959e92) shows tech-app saves on the same ticket as the office are routine

findings.title: Two-tech job completed from the office charges the primary, never the secondary who actually supplied
findings.scenario: 1. Handy Andy books an 85" job with Steve (primary) and Juan (secondary); ticket has 1x '85"-100" TV Full Motion Bracket'. 2. Juan brings the full-motion from his truck. Neither tech taps the 'Bracket supplier' card in the app (tech.html 1240-1247 / tech.js jobBracketSetSupplier) — the tech app would refuse completion until they did (tech.js 926 -> jobNeedsBracketSupplier 1943-1950), but they forget to close the job at all. 3. At end of day the office clicks 'Mark complete' on the dashboard (admin.html 3386 -> booking_update action=status, status=completed). 4. admin.js `case 'status'` (4144-4155) has NO jobNeedsBracketSupplier gate; the deduction block resolves supplier = bracket_supplied_by || technician_id (4357-4359) = Steve and debits Steve's full_motion (4362). Juan is never debited. If Steve's full_motion_qty was already 0 the decrement is clamped (admin.js 12278-12280) and NO count moves anywhere — the ledger row just carries a WARNING string. 5. Cross-hire variant: TK (Dom's) as secondary on a Handy Andy job supplying from his own truck — same outcome, TK's Dom's row untouched.
findings.wrongBy: Secondary tech shows +1 full_motion vs physical; primary shows -1 (or unchanged when clamped at 0). Net company count off by 1 whenever the primary is at 0.
findings.structuralCause: The 'who supplied it' rule is enforced only in the tech-app writer; the office completion writer re-implements the deduction without the gate and has no UI to record a supplier (admin.html has no bracket_supplied_by control). Two completion writers, one rule.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence in git; ba87325 (2026-07-07) deliberately made the office path fall back to technician_id with no supplier prompt

findings.title: Office completes a techless job: brackets logged 'unattributed', never debited, and no UI path ever attributes them
findings.scenario: 1. A widget booking loses the tech-slot race and lands with technician_id NULL (mirror.js 236-241; book.js 597-606 documents the Hasselman 2026-08-12 techless precedent). 2. Office phones a tech who does the job with a company Tilting bracket; the job never appears in any tech's app (tech.js scopeMine 61-65 requires primary or secondary = tech). 3. Office clicks 'Mark complete'. admin.js 4354 finds need.tilting=1, supplier resolves to null (4357-4359), so the else-branch at 4367-4382 inserts a bracket_usage_logs row with technician_id NULL and text 'inventory NOT deducted, needs manual attribution' and deliberately leaves bracket_deducted_at unset. No count moves. 4. Nothing surfaces that row: admin.html has no view of unattributed ledger rows, and the Assignment card is hidden on completed jobs (admin.html 3205 canAssign excludes 'completed'), so the office cannot simply assign the tech afterward. 5. The comment at 4372-4375 promises 'the line-item-edit reconciliation in bookingLineItemsSave still performs the real deduction' — but that reconcile is gated on the stamp being SET (4658), so an office edit later does NOT deduct either. The only repair is reopen -> assign -> re-complete, which nobody is prompted to do.
findings.wrongBy: The tech who did the job shows +N (ticket's bracket qty) vs physical, permanently; a ledger reconstruction that sums *_used without excluding technician_id IS NULL would over-count consumption that never moved a count.
findings.structuralCause: Attribution was deferred to 'manual attribution' with no manual attribution feature; the deferred-deduction promise depends on a stamp that this very branch refuses to set. Techless completions are a designed-for state (techless recovery code exists) but the inventory protocol has no branch for them.
findings.alreadyHappened: yes (partially): 3b1183a (2026-09-02) found this office path silently skipping deduction/stamp/log with no error from ba87325 (2026-07-07) onward — every office-completed techless job in that window is a missed debit with no trace; since 09-02 it leaves a ledger row but still no debit

findings.title: Hand-typed or catalog bracket lines outside the flat/tilt/full-motion vocabulary never debit (payroll treats them as a bracket sold, inventory does not)
findings.scenario: 1. On site the tech adds a line in the app for a second TV: 'Articulating bracket' $110 (or 'Swivel mount', 'Low profile bracket', 'Bracket', 'Extra bracket 55"') — the tech editor accepts free text (tech.html 1391-1392). 2. Tech completes. detectBracketQtys (tech.js 1750-1767 / admin.js 12239-12256) only matches /full.?motion/, /tilt/, /\bflat\b|fixed/ — 'articulating'/'swivel'/'low profile'/'bracket' match nothing, so need=0, no deduction, no stamp. 3. Payroll's matchItem reaches its last bracket rule at payroll.js 334 and classifies the same line as 'unrecognized bracket (material)' — the pay engine concludes a company bracket was sold ($0 labor), the inventory engine concludes nothing left the truck. 4. Same for the Handy Andy catalog option 'Mantel Mount' $195 (migration 0036 puts it in the bracket group): a company-supplied pull-down bracket with no inventory type at all. 5. Apple TV: the plain 'Apple TV installation' option and any hand-typed 'Apple TV mount' miss /apple\s*tv\b.*\bbracket\b/ (tech.js 1897-1899) even when a bracket was used.
findings.wrongBy: Supplier's count shows +1 per such line vs physical (the bracket type that physically left the truck — e.g. an articulating = full_motion — is never decremented); no ledger row.
findings.structuralCause: Consumption is inferred from regex over free-text line names with a three-word vocabulary; there is no structured bracket field on the ticket and no shared classifier with payroll, so the two engines disagree on whether a bracket was used.
findings.alreadyHappened: partial: payroll.js 324-325 records a real job (Jay Kapoor, Aug 2026) with hand-typed 'Custom bracket' ($250) and 'soundbar bracket' ($164) lines that inventory ignored; whether those were stocked flat/tilt/FM units is not recorded

findings.title: Failed inventory UPDATE is ignored, yet the ledger row and bracket_deducted_at stamp are still written — permanent missed debit that the ledger says happened
findings.scenario: 1. Tech completes a job with 1 Full Motion. tech.js adjustBracketInventory reads the row (1791-1793) and issues the UPDATE at 1800 — the returned {error} is discarded (same in admin.js 12282). 2. PostgREST returns an error object instead of throwing (supabase-js does not throw on a statement-level error, e.g. a statement timeout while the lambda is under load, or a transient 5xx from the pooler) — the count is unchanged. 3. The function proceeds to insert the bracket_usage_logs row at 1817 claiming full_motion_used=1 'auto-deduct (job completion)'. 4. Control returns to status(), which stamps bracket_deducted_at at 996. 5. The job is now terminal (tech.js 895) and stamped, so no path will ever deduct it; the ledger and the counter now disagree by exactly this bracket, and a ledger replay would 'confirm' the count is right.
findings.wrongBy: Supplier shows +N (the job's bracket qty) vs physical, and the ledger over-states consumption by the same N — the one shape of drift the 2026-08-21 ledger cannot detect.
findings.structuralCause: Counter write, ledger write and idempotency stamp are three unconditional, non-transactional steps; success of step 1 is never checked before steps 2 and 3 record it as done. The ledger is a side effect of the intent, not of the outcome.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence — would be invisible by construction (no error logged, ledger row present)

findings.title: Office re-clicks Mark complete while the first request is still sending the review email/SMS: both pass the stale stamp check and deduct twice
findings.scenario:
1. Office opens a job in the dashboard, clicks "✓ Mark complete", accepts the confirm(). public/admin.html:3386 awaits updateBooking(); the modal stays open and the button stays enabled until the await returns (updateBooking at 4073-4076 has no in-flight guard).
2. Request A: reads `existing` at api/admin.js:3994 (status assigned, no bracket_deducted_at). The 'status' branch at 4155 sets completed with no check that existing.status is not already completed (SETTABLE_STATUSES at 88 only validates the string). Updates bookings.status at 4245, inserts a status event, then AWAITS the review email and the Twilio SMS at 4254-4315 (plus two metadata writes) before it reaches the bracket block at 4349 — one to three seconds.
3. The screen does not change for two seconds, so the office clicks "✓ Mark complete" again and accepts the confirm again. Request B reads `existing` at 3994: status is already 'completed' but metadata.bracket_deducted_at is still absent because A has not reached 4365. B is not rejected.
4. A reaches 4349 (its stale copy has no stamp) → adjustBracketInventory(-1) at 4362 → reads the count at 12273, writes count−N at 12282 → stamps at 4365. B reaches 4349 (its copy also has no stamp) → adjustBracketInventory(-1) again → reads the count A just wrote, writes count−2N → stamps again.
5. Result: two 'auto-deduct (job completion (office))' ledger rows for one booking, two review texts to the customer, and the tech's count is down 2N for a job that used N.
Same outcome with a single click: if Vercel kills request A between the inventory write (12282) and the stamp (4365) — api/admin.js exports no maxDuration config, and 617379a records the status path being held open "until Vercel killed the function" by a hung SMS provider — the office sees an error toast, clicks again, and the retry deducts a second time.
findings.wrongBy: supplier tech shows N fewer of each bracket type than physical (N = the job's bracket qty), i.e. a 2-tilting job leaves the count 2 tilting too low
findings.structuralCause: The only idempotency guard is a JSONB stamp read at handler start and written ~10 awaits later (after third-party email/SMS calls), with no conditional UPDATE ... WHERE metadata->>'bracket_deducted_at' IS NULL, no rejection of status=completed on an already-completed booking, and a UI button that stays live for the whole request.
findings.alreadyHappened: No direct evidence of this exact interleaving in git. Same-shape incidents are on record: 617379a (2026-07-17) "a stale tab's re-tap re-texted the customer" through the tech status path and documents Vercel killing the status-path function mid-request; 1c2bd88 (2026-08-09) duplicate rows from a Save button left clickable through a slow async request. The 2026-09-03 incident (re-driving completion on jobs with no stamp) is the raw-SQL cousin of this mechanism.

findings.title: Double-click on Assign credits the delivered order twice (unconditional stamp, no credited marker, no ledger row); the same non-atomic ordering loses the credit permanently on a failed write
findings.scenario:
1. A delivered Walmart order (say 4 full_motion) sits in "Unassigned Walmart Orders". Owner picks Steve in the row's select and clicks Assign (public/admin.html:11383 → assignBracketDelivery 11399-11408), or uses the Assign modal (11315 → openAssignModal → confirmAssign 11068-11076). Neither handler disables the button or closes the modal until the await returns.
2. The click registers twice (double-click, or a second click when no toast has appeared after a second). Two POST bracket_assign requests are in flight.
3. Both requests select the purchase at api/admin.js:12538-12540 and both see technician_id null → both pass the check at 12542.
4. Both stamp technician_id at 12566-12568 — the UPDATE is `.eq('id', purchaseId)` only, not `.is('technician_id', null)`, so the second UPDATE matches too.
5. Both see status==='delivered' at 12587, both read inv at 12589-12591 and both write inv+4 at 12593-12597. If B's read lands after A's write, Steve is credited +8 for one box of 4.
6. bracketAssign writes no bracket_usage_logs row at all, so nothing in the ledger shows either credit; the owner sees two "✓ Assigned to Steve" toasts.
Partial-failure variant of the same ordering: stamp (12566) → twin delete (12575-12581) → credit throws (upErr/insErr thrown at 12598/12607) → 500. The order is now assigned with twins gone and the count unchanged; the retry is refused by 12542 ("already assigned") and the next cron sees assignedRow.status==='delivered' → wasDelivered=true → no credit (api/migrate.js:183, 192). The brackets are on Steve's truck and never on his count.
findings.wrongBy: tech shows +N (the order's full qty) more than physical on a double-click; N fewer than physical (never credited) on the failed-write variant
findings.structuralCause: Check-then-act on technician_id with an unconditional stamp UPDATE; stamp, twin delete and credit are three separate PostgREST calls with no transaction and no credited flag on bracket_purchases (wire_plate_purchases got one in migration 0041, brackets never did); no UI in-flight guard.

findings.title: Set Brackets modal is prefilled from page-render counts and writes all three columns back, silently reverting any deduction or credit that landed while the Inventory tab was open
findings.scenario:
1. Owner opens the Inventory tab at 4:00 pm. renderBrackets bakes each tech's counts into the Edit / Reorder onclick attributes (public/admin.html:11120 and 11129: openBracketEdit(id, name, flat, tilting, full_motion)).
2. At 4:20 pm Steve completes a job that uses 1 full_motion: api/tech.js:992 → 1800 writes full_motion 3→2 and a ledger row.
3. At 4:30 pm the owner, still on the same tab, clicks Edit on Steve. The modal is prefilled flat 5 / tilting 4 / full_motion 3 (openBracketEdit 11443-11452). They change flat to 6 because a stray flat bracket turned up in the truck, leave the other two alone, and Save. saveBracketCount 11470-11482 sends action:'set' with all three values.
4. bracketUpdate reads inv at api/admin.js:12099 (full_motion is 2 now), computes absolute flat 6 / tilting 4 / full_motion 3 at 12115-12118, and writes all three columns at 12140-12148. full_motion goes 2→3.
5. The ledger row at 12160-12168 reads "manual set by office: flat 5→6, full_motion 2→3" — the accidental revert is recorded as if it were intentional, so a later audit will trust it.
6. Steve's count says 3 full_motion; the truck has 2.
The plates / Apple TV "adjust" path has the same stale base: saveWirePlateCount and saveAppleTvBracketCount compute delta = typed − render-time cur (admin.html:11517, 11563), and bracketUpdate 'adjust' also rewrites flat/tilting/full_motion from the 12099 read (that window is one round trip).

findings.structuralCause: A manual correction is an absolute overwrite of all three columns from values captured at page render, with no updated_at/version compare-and-swap and no way to change only the field that was edited; the window is however long the tab has been open.
findings.alreadyHappened: no direct evidence of a specific reverted deduction; 7b166cb's message (2026-08-21) says TK's count drifted and manual sets left no history — before the ledger this class was invisible, after it the ledger row reads as intentional

findings.title: bracketSync credits inventory before it persists status='delivered', swallows the status-write error, and the 15-minute cron (no concurrency group) re-credits until the write sticks
findings.scenario:
1. The 10:15 cron run (.github/workflows/bracket-tracker.yml:11) scans the inboxes and POSTs order 2000149-… {status:'delivered', full_motion_qty:5} to bracket_sync. The order is assigned to TK (assignedRow at api/migrate.js:177), row status in_route.
2. bracketSync: wasDelivered=false, nowDelivered=true, totalQty=5 (183-192) → adjustBracketInventory credits TK +5 at 193 (read 86-88, write 96-100).
3. The status write at 203 fails (Supabase transient error, connection reset, or the function hitting maxDuration 60 at migrate.js:18). The error is pushed into `results` at 204, the handler still returns 200 at 299, the script logs and moves on (scripts/bracket-email-sync.mjs:327-329), and exits 0 (396-397). No alert.
4. The 10:30 run re-POSTs the identical payload (the script re-scans 45 days every run and keeps no state). The row still says in_route → 192 is true again → TK +5 again. This repeats every 15 minutes until 203 succeeds.
Overlap variant: bracket-tracker.yml has no `concurrency:` key (only estimate-escalation-check.yml:18 and tech-late-check.yml:24 have one). A workflow_dispatch — the manual status override step at yml:39-56, which then ALSO runs the full scan at 81-119 — launched while the cron run is mid-scan gives two runs POSTing the same order; if both read rows at 163-165 before either reaches 203, both see in_route and both credit at 193. The matched branch has the same shape (auto-assign update at 225, credit at 240).

findings.wrongBy: tech shows +N (the order's full qty) more than physical for every extra run that observed the row still in_route
findings.structuralCause: The idempotency latch is bracket_purchases.status, written AFTER the inventory move in a separate statement with the failure swallowed; there is no credited flag or idempotency key on bracket_purchases, no conditional UPDATE, no ledger row, and no workflow concurrency group to serialize runs.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Both techs on a two-tech job (or tech + office) tap Complete within the same ~200 ms: every guard is evaluated on a snapshot, the status UPDATE is unconditional, so both deduct
findings.scenario:
1. Two-tech job: Steve (primary) and Kregg (secondary), 3 tilting brackets, supplier recorded as Steve. Both phones show Mark Complete — scopeMine (api/tech.js:40-44) lets either tech advance the job, and the completion nudge (public/tech.html:1040-1050) fires on each phone once photos, payment and supplier are satisfied.
2. They tap within ~200 ms of each other as they pack up. Each phone disables only its own button (tech.html:1197; the nudge path at 2636 disables nothing).

4. Both pass TERMINAL_STATUS (895), the rank check, and the same-status replay guard (906) — all against their own stale copies. Both UPDATE bookings.status at 934 (`.eq('id', id)` only, no compare on the prior status).

The same interleaving works for office + tech: the office 'status' action goes from its read at api/admin.js:3994 to its UPDATE at 4245 with no intervening awaits; if the tech's read at 891 precedes 4245 and the office's read precedes the tech's 934, both deduct.
findings.wrongBy: supplier tech shows N fewer than physical (N = the job's bracket qty), with two 'auto-deduct (job completion)' ledger rows for one booking

findings.title: Whole-object metadata writes (line-item CAS claim, office assign/reopen/reschedule) can erase bracket_deducted_at written by a concurrent completion, re-arming a second deduction on the next reopen→recomplete
findings.scenario:
1. Tech completes a 2-full-motion job at 5:02:00 pm. api/tech.js status(): deducts at 992, then reads fresh metadata and writes {…, bracket_deducted_at} at 994-998 as an unconditional whole-object UPDATE.
2. The office has the same ticket's line-item editor open (loaded with li_rev 3 minutes ago) and clicks Save at 5:02:00. bookingLineItemsSave reads `existing` at api/admin.js:4518 (metadata {li_rev:3}, no stamp yet), passes the rev check, selects oldRows, then calls casBumpLiRev(db, id, existing.metadata, …) at 4590. casBumpLiRev (api/_lib/line-items.js:219-230) writes the WHOLE metadata object guarded only on li_rev=3; the comment at 214-218 admits any key stamped by another handler in that window is lost.
3. Interleaving: the tech's stamp write lands, then the office CAS lands (li_rev is still 3 → it matches) and replaces metadata with {li_rev:4, li_backups} — bracket_deducted_at is gone. The office's reconcile at 4658 checks its stale copy (no stamp) → nothing; the seal at 4697-4701 re-reads fresh metadata — which now lacks the stamp — and carries the loss forward.
4. A week later the office reopens the job to fix a payment detail (api/admin.js:4129-4143 spreads existing.metadata — still no stamp — into patch.metadata) and marks it complete again. At 4349 there is no stamp → adjustBracketInventory(−2) at 4362 → the job is deducted a second time. The ledger shows two 'auto-deduct' rows for one booking, a week apart.
The same erasure comes from bookingUpdate's own branches: assign (4124) and reopen (4141) build patch.metadata from the 3994 read and write it at 4245; an office reassign or reopen whose 3994→4245 window straddles the tech's 996 stamp write drops the stamp. Windows are one to three DB round trips (~50–300 ms).
findings.wrongBy: supplier tech shows N fewer than physical after the recomplete; or, if the erased stamp instead suppresses the line-item reconcile at 4658, N off in either direction
findings.structuralCause: The idempotency stamp lives in a JSONB blob that several handlers rewrite in full from a stale read (last writer wins); the seal was fixed to read fresh (comment at 4691-4694) but the claim and bookingUpdate's assign/reopen/reschedule branches were not, and no path uses a partial jsonb update or a dedicated column.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence of this exact interleaving; 1959e92 (Throckmorton, 2026-08-21) documents office and tech saving the same ticket five times in four minutes, so the concurrent-editor precondition is routine

findings.title: Every inventory mover is select→compute→update one round trip apart; two movers on the same tech row (cron credit vs job deduction, two completions for one tech) silently drop one move
findings.scenario:
1. 10:15:00.000 — the cron credits Steve's delivered order (+5 flat): api/migrate.js:86 reads flat 2, 96 writes 7.
2. 10:15:00.020 — Steve taps Complete on a 1-flat job: api/tech.js:1791 reads flat 2 (the cron's write has not landed yet), 1800 writes 1.
3. Whichever write lands second wins: 7 then 1 → count 1 (the +5 credit is lost); 1 then 7 → count 7 (the −1 deduction is lost). Physical stock is 6 either way. The tech.js path also writes a ledger row at 1817 claiming its deduction happened regardless of which write survived.
The same collision exists between an office completion of job A for Steve (api/admin.js:12273 read / 12282 write) and Steve's own completion of job B (tech.js:1791/1800), between bracketAssign's credit (12589/12593) and any deduction, and bracketUpdate (12099/12147) rewrites all three columns so it collides with everything.
There is no DB-side increment anywhere in the app: the only rpc calls in the repo are set_technician_pin and verify_technician_pin, and the only atomic bracket increment ever written is raw SQL (scripts/fix-juan-bracket-delivery.sql:34-41, `on conflict … do update set flat_qty = flat_qty + 5`).
findings.wrongBy: the lost move's full amount, in either direction, while the ledger (when one is written) still records the move as done
findings.structuralCause: bracket_inventory is a mutable counter mutated by four separate JS copies of read-modify-write with no SQL increment, no RPC, and no updated_at/version compare-and-swap; the window is one round trip per writer but the writers are numerous and uncoordinated.
findings.alreadyHappened: no evidence

findings.title: Tech-app line-item save rewrites the rows the detector reads but never reconciles inventory; only the office editor does
findings.scenario: 1. Widget job: '33"–59"' ×2 and 'Tilting (recommended)' qty 1 (customer said one bracket). 2. Tech taps Mark Complete: api/tech.js:980-997 runs detectBracketQtys over the rows → tilting 1 → adjustBracketInventory(-1) and stamps bracket_deducted_at. 3. On site the second TV also needed a company bracket. Tech opens Line items, taps + on the tilting row (public/tech.html:1385-1386; the row was seeded from the stored row at 1361) and Saves → job_line_items_save → api/tech.js:681-875 inserts the replacement row with quantity 2 (766-776), recomputes price/tax, bumps li_rev — the function contains no call to detectBracketQtys or adjustBracketInventory. 4. Later the office opens the ticket to add a discount and saves: api/admin.js:4660-4662 computes oldQtys from the DB rows (already 2) and newQtys (2) → equal → no reconcile. The gap is now permanent and invisible. 5. Opposite sign: the tech deletes the bracket row because the customer had their own → 1 was deducted, 0 used. 6. Compounding on a two-tech job: the tech later changes supplier; api/tech.js:1226 recomputes qtys from the CURRENT rows (2) and 1236-1240 restores 2 to the previous supplier although only 1 was ever debited.

findings.structuralCause: The consumed quantity is DERIVED from booking_line_items at completion time instead of being stored as a fact on the booking, so every writer of those rows must re-run the reconciliation — and only one of the three editors (office) was given it. Nothing records which qtys were actually deducted, so even the office reconcile can only compare row-vs-row, never row-vs-what-left-the-truck.
findings.alreadyHappened: No evidence of a specific job. 3b1183a (2026-09-02, 'Close two live bracket-inventory-tracking gaps') added the reconcile to api/admin.js only (git show --stat: 1 file changed); api/tech.js jobLineItemsSave was never given it.

findings.title: Estimate 'Upgrade to a Tilting/Full-Motion Bracket' upsell persists as a second bracket line beside the base bracket — two brackets deducted for one TV, and the TV-count clamp cannot fire across categories
findings.scenario: 1. Office builds a 1-TV New Booking ('TV Size: 60"-69"', 'Bracket: Flat') and clicks Send estimate. nbBracketUpsell (public/admin.html:16553-16573) adds the recommended add-on named 'Upgrade to a Tilting Bracket' (16567) priced at the tilting−flat delta (16563); it is posted as an upsell with qty 1 (16655). estimate_create stores the base selections verbatim as {description:'Bracket: Flat', qty:1} (api/admin.js:8671-8673). 2. Customer approves and ticks the upgrade: api/admin.js:10908-10912 concatenates the accepted upsell onto the base items and bookEstimateAppointment persists BOTH as booking_line_items (10798-10802). The manual convert path does the same (public/admin.html:10472-10478 → nbConvertLines → bookingCreate api/admin.js:3753-3760). Nothing removes or replaces 'Bracket: Flat'. 3. Tech brings ONE tilting bracket, mounts it, Mark Complete. detectBracketQtys: 'bracket: flat' → flat 1, 'upgrade to a tilting bracket' → tilting 1 (api/tech.js:1755-1758 / api/admin.js:12244-12247). clampBracketQtysToTvCount: tvUnits 1, total 2 > 1, but lineCounts.flat=1 and lineCounts.tilting=1 — no category with ≥2 lines → dup is empty → console.warn 'NOT clamping' and return false (api/_lib/line-items.js:186-191). adjustBracketInventory debits 1 flat AND 1 tilting. 4. Payroll pays $0 for both lines (api/_lib/payroll.js:314-317), so the pay review raises no flag; the office edit reconcile uses the same detector so it can never correct it. 5. Same shape when a tech or the office adds an on-site upgrade line ('Full motion upgrade +$35') beside the original selection instead of editing it.
findings.wrongBy: Supplier's flat count low by 1 per such job (a flat bracket that never left the truck is deducted); tilting correct. Per-job, systematic on every estimate whose customer accepted the bracket upgrade.
findings.structuralCause: The ticket has no structured 'bracket type × count' field. The estimate/upsell system models an upgrade as an additive price line, while the inventory detector treats every line containing a type word as a physical bracket. The Throckmorton clamp was designed for same-category duplicates only and explicitly stands down when the extra bracket is in a different category.
findings.alreadyHappened: No evidence found in git history or the 2026-09-03 incident.

findings.title: Tech line-item save persists the relabel 'In-Wall Wire Concealment', which neither detectWirePlateQty copy matches — plate never deducted while payroll still pays the behind-wall rate
findings.scenario: 1. Widget job with 'Yes, hide the wires BEHIND the wall' (public/widget.js:458 / 571). 2. Before completing, the tech opens Line items to add any line (e.g. a $50 soundbar). mkRow seeds EVERY existing row's name through liName (public/tech.html:1361); liRelabel rewrites the wire line to 'In-Wall Wire Concealment' (tech.html:576) and Save persists that string (tech.html:1391-1394 → api/tech.js:766-776). 3. Tech (or the office) marks complete. detectWirePlateQty requires /behind/ (gone) or /inwall/ (the persisted label is 'in-wall', hyphenated) → 0 plates (api/tech.js:1843-1844, api/admin.js:12227-12228). No deduction, no ledger row, wire_plate_deducted_at never stamped. 4. Payroll matches /\b(cord|wire)s?\b/ && /conceal/ and pays the $35/$45 behind-wall rate (api/_lib/payroll.js:297-300): the pay sheet says a plate job happened, inventory says it did not. 5. Office edits do NOT trigger this — liCleanLabel is display-only and the office save keeps the raw label (public/admin.html:3480-3496) — so the same ticket deducts a plate if only the office touched it and none if the tech touched it.

findings.structuralCause: Two regex vocabularies over one free-text label — payroll keys on 'conceal', inventory on 'behind'/'inwall' — and the tech app rewrites that label on every save. The relabel was declared 'payroll-safe' (bcb83ec) without checking the inventory detector, which is a separate copy in two files.
findings.alreadyHappened: Same failure class as the Max Segal job (3f5fec1, 2026-08-20: Gregory used a plate and his stock never moved because Dom's 'Inwall Concealment' wording did not match). The tech-side relabel has been persisted since bcb83ec (2026-07-02). No direct evidence for this exact 'In-Wall' wording.

findings.title: 'fixed' / 'flat' / 'tilt' substrings in free-text lines (handyman notes, Take-a-Call 'Other', correction jobs, customer's-own-bracket wording) deduct brackets that never existed; payroll classifies the same line as labor so nothing flags it
findings.scenario: 1. Secretary books a handyman job in New Booking or Take a Call: 'Handyman Labor: General — 3 hours (assemble flat-pack dresser)'. The label is built at public/admin.html:16236 with quantity = HOURS (3). 2. Tech completes. detectBracketQtys lowercases the name, /\bflat\b/ matches 'flat-pack' (hyphen is a word boundary) → flat += quantity 3 (api/tech.js:1754-1758). countTvUnits finds no TV-size line → tvUnits 0 → clamp returns false without trimming (api/_lib/line-items.js:150). adjustBracketInventory debits 3 flat brackets from the tech. 3. Payroll never sees a bracket: detectSpecial → 'handyman' (no TV base) and pays hours × $65 from the labor line (api/_lib/payroll.js:491-492, 653-666) — correct pay, so the weekly review gives no signal. 4. Same mechanism: '… — 2 hours (fixed the cabinet door)' → /fixed/ → flat −2; Take a Call 'Other: re-tilt the existing mount' (note appended to the label at admin.html:16249-16251) on a job whose bracket answer is 'I have my own bracket' → tilting −1 (only the literal phrase 'customer supplied' is skipped, api/tech.js:1755); office correction line 'Fixed TV that fell off the wall' or 'Install customer's own full motion mount' → flat/full_motion −1 while payroll prices the first as custom hourly (payroll.js:793-798) and the second as a $0 material (314-317). 5. Visible side-effect: on a two-tech job the tech app shows a '📦 Bracket' card and blocks Mark Complete until a supplier is chosen for the phantom bracket (api/tech.js:490-491, 1938-1950). Checked and consistent (no drift): Frame/Gallery in-box lines contain no type word → 0 in inventory and $15 in payroll; widget vs Take-a-Call naming ('Tilting (recommended)' vs 'Bracket: Tilting (recommended) ×2') detects identically.
findings.wrongBy: flat (or tilting/full_motion) count low by the line's quantity — for handyman lines that is the hours (2–4 brackets per job), not 1.
findings.structuralCause: Inventory infers a physical part from the presence of a word anywhere in a customer-facing description — no requirement that the row is a bracket option (option_id is stored but ignored), no precedence rules, and quantity taken from a column whose meaning differs by line kind (hours for labor, units for options). Payroll applies precedence (fees → dismount → handyman → exact catalog keys → wires → brackets) so the two systems classify the same text differently and the divergence is silent.
findings.alreadyHappened: Hand-typed lines carrying bracket words are documented on real tickets: 087f136 (2026-08-10, hand-typed 'Full Motion Mount' paid Gregory $65) and 278d3d7 (2026-08-10, 'Custom bracket' / 'soundbar bracket' on the Jay Kapoor job) — both surfaced as payroll incidents; no inventory evidence for the flat-pack/fixed handyman case.

findings.title: Throckmorton clamp only fires when the duplicate is worded as non-selection text; a hand-typed bare 'Tilting' / 'Flat' / 'Full Motion' line passes isSelectionLabel and double-deducts unclamped
findings.scenario: 1. Ticket: '98"+', '60"–69"', '33"–59"' ×2 (4 TVs) and 'Tilting (recommended)' ×3. 2. Office or tech, working from a stale screen, adds a second line typed just 'Tilting' ×3 — the Throckmorton edit war, but with the short wording people actually type. 3. Completion: detectBracketQtys → tilting 6. clampBracketQtysToTvCount: tvUnits 4, total 6 > 4, lineCounts.tilting = 2 — but isSelectionLabel('tilting') matches /^(?:flat|tilting\s*(?:\(recommended\))?|full\s*motion)…$/ (api/_lib/line-items.js:171) so nonSelection.tilting stays 0 → dup empty → 'NOT clamping' (189-190) → 6 tilting deducted for a 3-bracket job. The identical ticket worded 'Tilting Mounts' clamps to 4 (self-test 305-309, 332-336). 4. Payroll: both rows resolve to the 'tilting' catalog key at $0 (payroll.js:62), no flag.
findings.wrongBy: tilting count low by 3 (6 deducted, 3 used) — same magnitude as the 2026-08-21 Throckmorton double deduction.
findings.structuralCause: The safeguard encodes a guess about wording ('selection labels only come from the widget') rather than a fact (option_id, or a stored bracket count on the booking). li_rev makes the accidental duplicate rarer but a single editor can still add one, and the clamp's own escape hatch for standard+XL pairs is what lets the bare-word duplicate through.
findings.alreadyHappened: Throckmorton, 2026-08-21 (6 tilting deducted on a 3-bracket job) is the same mechanism with different wording; the clamp added in 1959e92 (2026-08-24) is tested only against 'Tilting Mounts'.

skepticVerdicts.reasoning:
Walked every cited line under C:\Users\andre\handy-andy-booking-repo; the sequence reproduces exactly and no guard interrupts it.

REPRODUCE-IN-CODE (all steps hold)
1. public/admin.html:11317-11324 — for role==='owner' the Status cell is a <select> with in_route/delivered/canceled whose onchange calls setBracketStatus(orderNum, id, value). bracketRow is reused for the archived "Delivered" table (11346-11349), so a delivered, tech-assigned order is downgradable. setBracketStatus (11050-11056) has no confirm() and posts straight to bracket_set_status.
2. api/admin.js:12058-12075 bracketSetStatus — owner-only; builds patch {status:'in_route', delivered_date:null}; because walmart_order_num is truthy it does .eq('walmart_order_num') across ALL rows for that order (no business filter). It never reads or touches bracket_inventory. No claw-back, no credited flag, no ledger row.
3. .github/workflows/bracket-tracker.yml runs scripts/bracket-email-sync.mjs on cron '*/15 * * * *'. The script scans INBOX only (line 180), since = now - LOOKBACK_DAYS (45 default, line 37/181), does not mutate the mailbox (header comment lines 15-17), mergeByOrder (98-114) keeps the highest status and max quantities, and POSTs every distinct order every run (311-330). The only skip is qty===0 && status==='in_route' (319), which a delivered payload never hits. walmart-parse.mjs detectStatus (66-74) returns 'delivered' for "Your package arrived"/"completed your delivery", and parseWalmartEmails sets delivered_date = today (198).
4. api/migrate.js bracketSync: assignedRow = row with technician_id (177). wasDelivered = assignedRow.status==='delivered' → false after the downgrade (183); nowDelivered = true (184); totalQty>0 → line 192-194 calls adjustBracketInventory with the FULL order quantities. adjustBracketInventory (83-101) is a read-then-write += on bracket_inventory with clamp-at-zero only; grep confirms migrate.js contains zero bracket_usage_logs writes. upgrades('in_route') is true (rank 0→1), so statusPatch() (170-175) sets status='delivered' + delivered_date and line 203 persists it. Result: Greg +full qty a second time, status silently reverts, no ledger row for either credit.

ALREADY-GUARDED (none apply)
- bracket_purchases has no credited/inventory_applied column: migrations 0029/0030/0056/0057 are the only ones touching it (id, business_id, technician_id nullable, qtys, status, order_date, delivered_date, order_url, order_total, estimated_delivery). The `credited` one-way latch exists ONLY on wire_plate_purchases (0041; admin.js:12032-12044 and migrate.js:435-506 explicitly lock status once credited and claw back on cancel). Brackets got no equivalent.
- The upgrade-only rule (BRACKET_STATUS_RANK, migrate.js:79/169) is what re-arms the credit, not what prevents it.
- The clamp only blocks negatives; over-credit is unaffected. Twin-row deletion is irrelevant (single assigned row). li_rev/bracket_deducted_at live on bookings, not purchases.
- Commit 3b1183a (2026-09-02 "Close two live bracket-inventory-tracking gaps") changed only bookingUpdate completion and bookingLineItemsSave; it never touches purchase status or the sync.
- Only DB triggers on bracket_purchases are set_updated_at (0029:37). No trigger reconciles inventory.
- The other bracket_purchases writers (bracketAssign 12527-12617, manual purchase logger ~12417-12455, tech.js reads only) don't add any idempotency marker the sync could check.

OPERATIONAL-REALITY (nothing impossible required)
The owner is exactly the role the dropdown is shown to; downgrading a delivered order is a one-click, unconfirmed action on a row the UI shows him. The delivery email sits in the Walmart mailbox INBOX (GMAIL_USER_2 domstvmounting@) for the full 45-day window unless someone archives it; the script's own comment (174-179) says INBOX retention is the design assumption.
